It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.

papers.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
papers.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.

papers.title: KUDEX: A Zero-Shot Decompositional Framework for Logical Analysis in Natural Language
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at generating fluent text, they often struggle with multi-step logical reasoning with inferential connections among statements. We introduce KUDEX (Knowledge-Upward-Downward Reasoning Extension), a novel zero-shot, decompositional framework for analyzing and verifying logical relationships in natural language. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on surface-level entailment checks, KUDEX leverages LLMs to decompose reasoning into atomic primitives and constructs transparent reasoning graphs that serve both as execution traces and audit logs. Our framework includes a general prompt adaptation pipeline that adapts to diverse reasoning tasks without additional fine-tuning or domain-specific pipelines. Through comprehensive experiments on benchmarks across four domains, we demonstrate that KUDEX provides superior performance compared to existing methods, offering a more granular and robust framework for assessing logical relationships between statements.

papers.title: Interpreting JWST UV luminosity functions and angular correlation functions via a "universal language" for high-redshift galaxies
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) found more bright $z\gtrsim10$ galaxies than expected before its launch. No consensus has emerged on whether difficulties in reproducing them stem from missing physics, simplifying assumptions that break down at the highest redshifts, or model mis-calibration. This is complicated because most galaxy models cannot be compared like-to-like, and models invoking different physical processes can make similar predictions for compressed summaries such as ultraviolet luminosity functions (UV LFs). Here we describe galaxy populations in a universal language: a chain of physically and empirically motivated conditional distributions linking halo mass, stellar mass, star formation rate and UV magnitude, defined consistently across models and data. We build a broad prior from fits to five hydrodynamic simulations, which predict very different high-redshift galaxy populations. We infer the parameters of this flexible galaxy model from $z>6$ JWST observations of UV LFs and angular correlation functions (ACFs). Including the mass-complete ACFs disfavors a large scatter around the stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR). With simulation-based priors, the star-forming main sequence (SFMS) is described by a star-formation timescale of about one halo dynamical time, and the scatter around the SFMS increases toward lower stellar masses. The SFMS scatter is the main source of stochasticity in UV magnitude at fixed halo mass, accounting for a median $\sim$61% of the variance at $M_{\rm UV}=-20$ (SHMR scatter: $\sim$36%). Bayesian model selection finds no evidence for redshift evolution of the SHMR or for an SFMS slope different from unity. At $z\sim20$, our fiducial model predicts UV LFs orders of magnitude below estimates from photometric candidates. A consensus on the discrepant UV LF estimates at $z\geq14$ is needed to determine whether model extensions are required.

papers.title: Scaling Channel-Adaptive Self-Supervised Learning
papers.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervised pre-training of foundation models for natural images have made them a popular choice for various visual systems and applications. Self-supervised strategies are also promising in non-RGB scientific imaging domains such as in biology, medical and satellite imagery, but their broader application is hampered by heterogeneity in channel composition and semantics between relevant datasets: two datasets may contain different numbers of channels, and these may reveal distinct aspects of an object or scene. Recent works on channel adaptive strategies report substantial advantages for those that account for variable channel compositions without sacrificing the ability to jointly encode channels; yet, how these strategies behave at scale remains unclear. We here show that, surprisingly, trained across large-scale datasets, independent-encoding of channels outperforms joint-encoding methods by a substantial margin. We validate this result along an extensive set of experiments on various datasets from cell microscopy to geospatial imagery. Our DINO BoC approach sets a new state-of-the-art across challenging benchmarks, including generalization to out-of-distribution tasks and unseen channel combinations. We open-source code and model weights for a new general-purpose feature extractor for fluorescent microscopy.

papers.title: Flexible ground-state search algorithm on hybrid Clifford-tensor network manifolds
papers.abstract: Tensor network algorithms face challenges in highly entangled regimes, such as systems with periodic boundary conditions (PBC), long-range interactions, or higher dimensions, where the required bond dimension quickly renders computations infeasible. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel approach that integrates the stabilizer formalism directly into the traditional density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm. While previous methods have used Clifford unitaries to minimize ground-state entanglement, fundamentally limited to distilling that away utilizing local two-qubit operations, our framework optimizes Clifford transformations to minimize the state's energy. We benchmark our method against standard DMRG at fixed bond dimensions for the Ising model on a ring (including long-range interactions) and on a torus. We observe systematic gains in models with local interactions - as drastic as a factor of 40 decrease in bond dimension in two dimensions. Our algorithm is readily implementable in standard DMRG codes and provides a practical way to substantially reduce algorithm costs, paving the way for large-scale simulation at volumes beyond what is presently achievable.

papers.title: Mapping the Afterlife of Future Work Statements in NLP Research
papers.abstract: Future work statements are one of the few places in scientific papers where authors explicitly describe what they think should happen next. We study what happens to such statements after publication. We construct a dataset of 72,070 future work items extracted from 23,113 ACL Anthology papers published between 1979 and 2025, categorize them by type, retrieve candidate follow-up papers through citation-based and content-based search, and use LLM-based judgments to assess whether later papers pursue the proposed directions. Using this resource, we analyze patterns across time, venues, categories, themes, and authors. We find that many items are later addressed, often within a few years, with clear differences across types and themes and a largely community-driven pattern. Our results suggest that future work statements provide useful evidence for studying how research directions develop in NLP. To support further research, we release our dataset at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20385239.

papers.title: Multi-Assay Antibody Developability Prediction with Shared Structure-Language Representations
papers.abstract: Early assessment of antibody developability is critical in drug discovery, but computational approaches remain limited by the scarcity of experimental data. We explore two strategies for working within that limit. First, we designed per-residue physicochemical descriptors encoding the local structural environment, including new terms such as directional charge asymmetry and screened electrostatic potential. These feed a convolutional network, combined with protein language model (PLM) embeddings in a two-stream architecture: the two are encoded and predicted independently and merged only at the prediction stage. Second, a shared trunk with per-assay heads passes information between related assays. Both are implemented in the Multi-Assay Developability Model (MADM) and evaluated on eight assays: HIC, heparin affinity (HAC), AC-SINS, and polyspecificity ELISA against BVP, dsDNA, insulin, ovalbumin and soluble membrane proteins (SMP), with labels from 29 open sources. Structural descriptors match or exceed PLM embeddings (AbLang2, ESM2) on several assays; combining the streams gives a small but consistent gain in accuracy and reduces seed-to-seed variance. Multi-assay training raises Spearman rho for ovalbumin and SMP by about 0.1, where assays correlate and share sequence space. Under cluster-split cross-validation the strongest results are for HAC, ovalbumin, insulin, SMP and HIC (rho = 0.70-0.82); AC-SINS, BVP and dsDNA are weaker (0.50-0.55). In these three, sequence clusters largely coincide with data source, so a held-out fold measures transfer to differently calibrated measurements as well as to new sequences. On the 80-antibody GDPa3 hold-out, performance falls by rho around 0.1 for all but SMP (0.22). Transfer to the VHH panel of Ginkgo GDPa5 gives comparable results, and scFv validation against binary SMP labels yields F1 = 0.89, AUC = 0.95.

papers.title: Exposing and overcoming the polarizability pathology of the Fermi-Omont pseudopotential
papers.abstract: Any realistic electron-atom or ion-atom potential energy function contains a long-range contribution from the atomic polarizability which gives a $1/r^4$ long-range tail. This modifies the well-known Wigner threshold law for orbital momenta $L>0$, causing these $L\neq 0$ scattering phase shifts to vary linearly in energy instead of as $k^{2L+1}$. The $L>0$ Fermi-Omont zero-range pseudopotentials are erroneously divergent at zero energy due to this modification, a divergence deriving from very long-range physics that should not be incorporated into a Dirac delta function. Here, we investigate some alternative scenario for repairing this pathological behavior to obtain smooth and accurate potential energy curves calculated using the Fermi-Omont pseudopotential concept, with some systematic benchmarking tests for comparison.

papers.title: Identification and external validation of the sets of 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, and 24-hour CGM motifs
papers.abstract: There is growing interest in using CGM for purposes other than those initially intended. Recent work of Lobo et al. identified $Ω$: a set of motifs such that almost any daily CGM profile (the 24-hour CGM time series starting at midnight) can be classified - matched to a motif in $Ω$. This work generalizes the prior work by identifying sets of motifs for 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, and 24-hr CGM profiles where an $x$-hr CGM profile does not have to be 24 hours in length, and does not have to start at midnight. The prior work methods are modified to identify the five new sets of motifs using data from the same 6 studies in the original work. The newly identified sets were subjected to rigorous external validation using a data set comprised of data from 21 studies (3,455 subjects, 289,592 days of CGM data). The external validation data set has both temporal and geographic transportability and addresses limitations of the data set used to define the five new sets of motifs. The results of the external validation indicate that the prior work generalizes well: the performance of each $x$-hr set of motifs on the external validation set is almost identical to that obtained for $Ω$. The generalization of the original work broadens the potential use cases of the framework to include short term predictions (e.g., impending hypoglycemia) and diagnostics which rely on detecting changes in CGM time series which are less than 24 hours in length.

papers.title: Ab initio calculations of ${\barδ_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
papers.abstract: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $β$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\barδ_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(α^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\barδ_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(α^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $δV_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

papers.title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
papers.abstract: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_σ$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{σ,{\rm eff}} = 2m_π$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.

papers.title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
papers.abstract: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.

papers.title: Gapless Nature of Spin Liquid in the $S=1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet with Neural-Network Quantum States
papers.abstract: Whether the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet hosts a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ or a gapless $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid remains a central open question in frustrated magnetism. Here, we address this question by directly computing the triplet gap with a neural-network quantum state that does not presuppose any specific spin-liquid structure. Applying a time-reversal symmetric transformer-based ansatz to clusters of up to $768$ sites, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies on two-dimensional lattices with periodic boundary conditions and estimate an energy per site of $-0.43873(12)$ in the thermodynamic limit. Finite-size scaling of the magnetic order parameter and triplet excitation gap shows that both extrapolate to zero in the thermodynamic limit. Together, these results provide independent and direct evidence of a gapless spin-liquid ground state, consistent with the $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid. More broadly, they demonstrate that neural-network quantum states can resolve ground-state properties of frustrated quantum magnets that remain challenging for conventional numerical methods.

papers.title: Universal Quantum Computation in a Wigner's Friend Framework
papers.abstract: The Wigner's Friend thought experiment illustrates a core tension in quantum mechanics: an observer inside an isolated laboratory (the Friend) measures a definite outcome, while an external observer (Wigner) describes the laboratory as a coherent superposition. Here we show that this discrepancy, usually studied as a conflict between descriptions, has a direct computational consequence. We namely propose a protocol by which Wigner can turn the Friend's laboratory into a universal quantum computer, whereby the Friend is restricted to apply simple classical operations within the laboratory. We also experimentally implement a proof-of-principle demonstration of this protocol for single-qubit gates using single photons. By recasting the coherence between incompatible descriptions as a computational resource, we thus link the foundations of quantum measurement to quantum computation.

papers.title: Metamorphic Testing of Quantum Software based on Stabilizer States
papers.abstract: A major challenge in quantum computing is to systematically check if a quantum program implements its desired functionality. For classical programs, testing is widely used; each test case comprises a pair of sample input and expected output to be compared with the actual output. To increase the number of test cases, however, one has to solve the test-oracle problem: for each additional test input one has to know the correct output. Metamorphic testing tackles this problem by utilizing metamorphic relations between input and output domains to automatically derive new test cases from existing ones. However, adapting metamorphic testing to the quantum realm is not straightforward, since quantum states cannot be directly inspected. We propose a framework of quantum metamorphic testing (QMT) in which the metamorphic relations incorporate the measurement procedures required to assess quantum outputs. We apply our QMT framework to testing the preparation of stabilizer states, which are central to protocols like measurement-based quantum computing or quantum error correction. We utilize structural properties of stabilizer states to systematically derive measurement circuits for new test cases from existing ones. We implement this framework in Qiskit, and demonstrate that it reduces by an order of magnitude the testing run time compared to testing with randomly generated input states. We further show effectiveness by revealing synthetic program faults injected by circuit mutations, as well as a real bug in the Qiskit compiler.

papers.title: Generalised global symmetries of 6d SCFTs on a circle from the blow-up equations
papers.abstract: We study 6d $(1,0)$ SCFTs on a circle, possibly twisted, through the blow-up equations of their 5d descriptions. For every theory we consider, we construct the explicit map between the 6d and 5d frames, including the ratio $r$ of the Kaluza--Klein (KK) mass to the instanton mass, which depends on the frame and not only on the twist. Our main result is that the higher-form symmetries of these theories, their mixed anomalies and 2-groups can all be read off from the fluxes through the exceptional curve of the blown-up $\mathbb{C}^2$. The flux sectors are the 't$~$Hooft sectors of the 5d 1-form symmetries. On the tensor fluxes, the 6d Green--Schwarz couplings fix the weights, whose fractional exponents we read as the mixed anomalies of the 6d 2-form symmetry with the KK $\mathrm{U}(1)$, gravity, flavour and $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$. The fluxes forced in each sector decide between a 2-group and a mixed anomaly. For instance, the twisted frames $\mathfrak{su}(4)_{0,4}+4Λ^2$ carry a non-split $\mathbb{Z}_4$ 2-group, while, in $\mathfrak{su}(4)_2+4Λ^2$ and $\mathfrak{su}(4)_6+2Λ^2$, the instanton symmetry is locked to the flavour centre and only a mixed anomaly remains. The same method applies to the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ gauging of two, three and four copies of the $E_1$ theory, which describes, respectively, $\mathrm{SU}(4)_0$, pure $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$ and the untwisted $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ KK theory. There, the fluxes exhibit the extensions of 1-form symmetries inherited from the $E_1$ 2-groups, identify the states that break each accidental 1-form symmetry and the background to which it is locked, and give the 5d 2-group to which the $S_3$-invariant 6d 3-group reduces.

papers.title: Quadratic Sum Rules for Scalar Amplitudes
papers.abstract: Kleiss--Kuijf and Bern--Carrasco--Johansson relations, and their string monodromy generalizations, have long provided some of the most powerful and useful constraints on partial amplitudes. Motivated by their success, we uncover a new class of quadratic-sum rules that connect scalar amplitudes at different multiplicities. Combining recursion, kinematic shifts, and symbolic regression, we establish them for the nonlinear sigma model and its string-inspired extensions. We then extend these relations to diagonal elements of the inverse Kawai--Lewellen--Tye matrix and subsequently to planar scalar theories with nonderivative interactions and general propagators.

papers.title: Thermal emission spectroscopy of the ultra-hot Jupiter HAT-P-70b: NIRPS constraints on its refractory and volatile content
authors: Rillck Guilherme de Souza Barros de Amorim
papers.abstract: Context. The chemical makeup of exoplanets provides insight into their origins and internal structures. High dayside temperatures on ultra-hot Jupiters vaporise refractory species and dissociate volatile molecules such as water. Cooler nightsides enable condensation (e.g. Fe) and cold-trapping (e.g. Ti), as compounds transition out of the gas phase. These contrasting conditions make dayside emission spectra a probe of both elemental inventories and atmospheric chemistry in the gas. Aim. We characterise the dayside atmosphere of the ultra-hot Jupiter HAT-P-70b via thermal emission spectroscopy, constraining its refractory and volatile budget and assessing thermal dissociation and cold-trapping. We focus on the abundances of rock-forming elements (Fe, Si, and Mg) and the depletion or survival of Ti and H2O. Methods. We analyse secondary-eclipse observations of HAT-P-70b acquired with NIRPS. From the emission spectrum, we infer the planet's atmospheric thermal structure and composition using a well-mixed retrieval framework. Results. We detect emission signatures from Fe, Mg, V, Si, and OH, but no significant H2O signal. The presence of OH and absence of water indicate strong thermal dissociation, with water likely depleted by more than 90% in the probed layers. The retrieved temperature profile shows a pronounced thermal inversion. Elemental abundance ratios (Fe/Si, Mg/Si, V/Si) are broadly consistent with solar-like composition, while titanium appears sub-solar, possibly due to partial condensation and nightside cold-trapping. Conclusions. HAT-P-70b's dayside atmosphere is dominated by refractory species and strong thermal processes. The detection of OH and absence of H2O indicate efficient water dissociation, while sub-solar titanium suggests nightside cold-trapping. Refractory element ratios are consistent with solar values, supporting a link between planetary and stellar compositions.

papers.title: Quantum Cooling by Classical Shadows
papers.abstract: Cooling to ground states of many-body Hamiltonians by imaginary-time evolution is central to quantum simulation, but its non-unitary aspect prevents direct implementation on a quantum computer. Existing routes restore it by importing structure from outside the intrinsic quantum dynamics, e.g. by parameter estimation on many copies or recursive compilation. Here, we show that a single randomized snapshot of the quantum many-body system is sufficient to steer the state along the cooling direction on average. Our algorithm, shadow chain, uses randomized measurements to collapse the state to its classical record, which fixes the next unitary update. Snapshots across steps form a trajectory that is a quantum-executable sample of an auxiliary-field path integral; fluctuations among trajectories are exponentially suppressed in system size. With the randomness supplied intrinsically by the Born measurement rule, the trajectories sample themselves rather than going through external accept-reject steps. The resulting algorithm is ansatz-free and exact upon extrapolation to the continuous limit, with the exponential cost confined only to system size rather than temperature.

papers.title: Black Hole Superradiance and the Gravitational Auger Effect
papers.abstract: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of nature's light degrees of freedom. In the vicinity of a spinning black hole, it exponentially amplifies ultralight bosons from vacuum fluctuations to a macroscopic cloud of enormous occupation number. Observational superradiance effects - modified black-hole spins, gravitational-wave and coherent boson emission - are known to depend sensitively on bosonic self-interactions as induced by a quartic, $λϕ^4$. Here we point out that purely gravitational interactions within the cloud significantly modify superradiance dynamics, through an analog of the Auger effect. Moreover, we identify nontrivial evolution of the superradiant levels beyond the first, driven by scattering into even higher levels and their radial overtones. For the QCD axion, the irreducible gravitational coupling rapidly dissipates the first superradiant level after it reaches saturation, through scalar emission and absorption by the black hole, while truncating the growth of higher levels. This can dramatically suppress the observability of continuous gravitational-wave signals or signatures in late binary inspirals. Black hole spin-down remains more robust, but for higher modes begins earlier and proceeds more slowly, requiring revision of existing limits.

papers.title: Constants and Nonperturbative Corrections in $V^{5,2}$ Theories
papers.abstract: We study perturbative and exponentially small corrections to the on-shell effective twisted superpotentials of two three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories associated with free and fixed-locus cyclic quotients of the non-toric Sasaki-Einstein manifold $V^{5,2}$. These are the two-node Chern-Simons theory at levels $(k,-k)$ and the one-node flavored theory with $N_f$ fundamental pairs, respectively. At superconformal chemical potentials, we propose the Chern-Simons counterpart of the all-order perturbative expression for the flavored theory and obtain convergent integral representations for the rank-independent constants of both theories. At integer parameters, these constants admit explicit evaluations involving finite sums of Clausen functions and $ζ(3)$, while their large-parameter expansions Borel sum to the defining integrals. At $k=1,3$ and $N_f=1,3$, we conjecture complete exponential remainders expressed through Eichler integrals of weight-four Eisenstein series. Supported by high-precision Bethe solutions, the resulting completions coincide at unit quotient order but differ at order three. We determine the minimal modular levels of the Eisenstein generators and establish convergence and natural boundaries for their primitives. Within the relative M-theory localization prescription, a complementary bulk analysis recovers the Chern-Simons shifted rank and constant in the $b\to0^+$ limit of the squashed-sphere partition function. We propose a generalization incorporating fixed-locus contributions that yields the corresponding flavored-theory result. The two theories therefore share a modular structure in their nonperturbative coefficient laws, but distinct perturbative shifts and exponential corrections resolve differences invisible in their common leading $N^{3/2}$ behavior.

papers.title: Rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models from a tetrality web
papers.abstract: We construct rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising (TIM) models by using different chiral symmetries to prepare their folded boundary states. We use a moving up procedure which extends the product theory to an auxiliary coset with an $S_3$ automorphism group, where permutations give twisted Cardy states. We complement this with a moving down approach which reduces to the $S_3$ invariant algebra. Overall, these procedures uncover a tetrality web relating four different theories. Pulling back ordinary Cardy states of the smallest theory in the web to the physical tensor product system gives eighteen factorized interfaces and six transmitting interfaces. The latter agree with four transposition and two 3-cycle twisted boundaries in the largest theory. They include Gaiotto's RG wall and the interface obtained by fusing an Ising duality line into it. The six interfaces carry the regular action of the TIM fusion ring and have the same energy transmission coefficient, $35/48$. Their boundary entropies, bulk correlations and operator spectra distinguish them. We calculate these observables and the complete annulus amplitudes between the twenty four boundaries.

papers.title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $β$ decays using effective field theory
papers.abstract: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $β$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\barδ_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $δV_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.

papers.title: Optimal Frobenius light cones for power-law systems in any dimension
papers.abstract: We prove optimal Frobenius Lieb-Robinson bounds for power-law systems with power-law exponent $α$ in any dimension $d$, in particular showing that the algebraic to linear light cone transition occurs at $α=d+1$. The proof uses a spectral clipping method and concentration result to allow for running a multiscale operator-norm argument which produces the optimal Frobenius norm exponent. Additionally, we prove there is a Frobenius light cone transition from polylogarithmic to algebraic at the summability threshold $α=d$, and a transition from decaying in volume to non-decaying in volume at $α=d/2$.

papers.title: Probing the QCD Conformal Window with Four-Quark Operators
papers.abstract: The infrared fate of QCD-like theories and their conformal window for different numbers or flavours and colour remains an open question with applications ranging from high-energy to condensed-matter systems. A hallmark of phase transitions from a conformal to symmetry breaking phase can be the presence of classically irrelevant operators that provide relevant deformation in the infrared. We investigate this scenario by computing anomalous dimensions of all four-quark operators, with or without chiral symmetry, at four-loop order as well as the dimension-six gluonic operator at three loops in Veneziano QCD. Scaling dimensions are derived in a systematic conformal expansion. These results are improved with various resummation techniques and we estimate their uncertainties. We find no concrete evidence for a composite operator effectively describing a merger with the QCD fixed point.

papers.title: Gravitational Memory Correlators and BMS Symmetry
papers.abstract: We compute the n-point memory and mixed energy-memory correlators for scalar decay into gravitons using the in-in formalism at leading order in perturbative quantum gravity. We obtain compact results for arbitrary n and explicitly verify the supertranslation flux balance relation between memory, energy, and Bondi mass detectors, realizing asymptotic symmetry constraints on infrared-finite observables.

papers.title: Schwarzschild scattering from CFT
papers.abstract: We show that retarded CFT correlators on $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{S}^2$ in a state described by the small black hole in AdS$_4$ can be used to derive asymptotically flat Schwarzschild partial-wave S-matrix elements, including its spectrum of quasinormal modes. This is achieved by identifying a class of operators for which the dual bulk fields behave as plane waves near the AdS boundary for sufficiently high frequencies. For such operators there is a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and reflection coefficients which behaves gracefully in the flat space limit, $L\to \infty$. These include spin-1, spin-2, and conformally coupled scalars. We provide a simple toy model that captures how dissipative QNMs can appear for short times inside Hermitian systems, closely resembling the small black hole in AdS.

papers.title: Landau's problems through ratios of $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Very recently, Lee announced a proof of the Twin Prime Conjecture assuming the Ratios Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function. We obtain conditional asymptotic formulas with power-saving errors for each of Landau's four prime problems. In the function field setting, using Sawin's estimates for factorization functions in squarefree progressions and a discriminant cohomology argument, we obtain unconditional Goldbach and prime-pair asymptotics over sufficiently large fixed odd fields, including prime fields. Similar results may be possible for other problems in analytic number theory.

papers.title: Sensitivity of the SHiP experiment at CERN to sterile-neutrino-induced oscillations
papers.abstract:
The SHiP experiment, approved for the high-intensity beam-dump facility in the ECN3 hall at the CERN SPS in the North Area, will record neutrino interactions both in its scattering and neutrino detector (SND) and, about \SI{70}{m} further downstream, in its calorimeter system. We show that the baseline SHiP detector configuration therefore forms a two-baseline experiment for oscillations induced by a sterile neutrino. From a 	extsc{Geant4} simulation of 	extsc{Genie}-generated interactions we derive the energy response of both stations to $
ue$ and $
umu$ charged-current (CC) interactions and the separation of $
ue$~CC events from the neutral-current $\pizero$ background, and fold them into a near/far disappearance analysis with a $20\%$ flux-shape uncertainty and a $1\%$ far/near normalisation uncertainty. For $6	imes10^{20}$ protons on target, the projected $95\%$~CL median sensitivities are $\Umufour\simeq\UmuLimit$ at $\mfour\simeq\UmuLimitMass$~eV and $\Uefour\simeq\UeLimit$ at $\mfour\simeq\UeLimitMass$~eV. In the muon channel this lies below existing $
umu$-disappearance limits for $\DnineLow\lesssim\mfour\lesssim\DnineHigh$~eV.

papers.title: A treatment of d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians with noninteger quantum numbers and their connection to the radial momentum operator
papers.abstract: The Bagci-Hoggan exponential-type orbitals, the generalization of Coulomb-Sturmians to noninteger quantum numbers, were recently identified as d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians. In the present study, this identification is treated in detail. The radial differential equation for these orbitals is derived directly from their closed form. It represents the general Coulomb-Sturmian differential equation for quantum numbers with real values. The solution is verified through a power series representation and a first-order matrix form based on the Green's function of the radial Laplacian. New transformation relationships between these orbitals and Slater-type orbitals with noninteger principal quantum numbers are established. The radial differential equation is expressed in terms of the radial momentum operator. The expectation values of the position and radial momentum operators are obtained in closed form. The radial and Heisenberg uncertainty products, the Shannon entropy and the Fisher information are derived in general form.

papers.title: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Recent advances in audio-driven avatar video generation have enabled increasingly realistic synthesis, yet achieving precise lip-audio synchronization, natural, human-like motion, and visual consistency over long sequences remains challenging. We present LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6, which builds on LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 to improve expressive naturalness and reduce error accumulation during extended generation, e.g., exaggerated lip movements and overly red, temporally unstable lip coloration, enhance the naturalness of facial expressions and coordinated head and body movements. These improvements are driven by a refined post-training pipeline that integrates reinforcement learning, improved classifier-free guidance strategies for DMD-based few-step distillation, long-video rollouts, and on-policy distillation. Together, these refinements improve expressive realism and enable the generation of videos exceeding 10 minutes while maintaining visual quality and temporal consistency. Arena evaluations show that LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 outperforms its predecessor and competing commercial audio-driven avatar models, demonstrating the effectiveness of the improved post-training pipeline.

papers.title: Observables and Symmetries in Causal Fermion System
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay of observables and symmetries in the framework of causal fermion systems (CFS). We show that position observables transform covariantly under unitary symmetries and for static CFS we derive their Heisenberg-type evolution. To give these results a geometric interpretation, we establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of CFS constructed from solutions of the Dirac equation. The crucial link is provided by the Dirac equation itself, which relates the infinitesimal generators of the geometric and CFS symmetries. In static spacetimes, this allows us to identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian.

papers.title: What explainable deep learning reveals about wall-bounded turbulence: insights from conditional surprisal
papers.abstract: Explainable deep learning (XDL) has identified regions of wall turbulence important for prediction that are only partly captured by classical coherent-structure criteria. We examine turbulent channel flow at friction Reynolds numbers $Re_τ\simeq125$ and $550$ by comparing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with conditional surprisal, which quantifies how unexpected an observed velocity transition is given its initial state. Although SHAP selection favours energetic fluid and largely overlaps classical masks, selected fluid outside these masks is less energetic but exhibits higher surprisal. Near the wall, at comparable fluctuation energy and wall distance, high-surprisal voxels outside classical masks are approximately 11 and 5 times more likely to be selected by SHAP than low-surprisal voxels, respectively. Within classical masks, the factor is about 1.3. SHAP-selected structures containing paired high- and low-speed regions exhibit surprisal maxima near their internal $u=0$ interfaces, where transverse velocity fluctuations remain nonzero. These interfaces contain vortical and SHAP-only regions, with the latter accounting for more than half of their reconstructed area. In part of the buffer layer, the SHAP-only portions have higher mean surprisal than the vortical portions. However, comparison with generic $u=0$ surfaces indicates that much of the raw interfacial surprisal excess is associated with surrounding fluctuation energy; after energy matching, the equally weighted surface comparison is statistically compatible with unity on the retained common support. Together, these results show how state-conditioned velocity transitions complement instantaneous structure-identification criteria in characterizing SHAP-selected flow.

papers.title: Functional nestedness of soil nematode communities across Europe: integrating morphological counts and eDNA reads
papers.abstract: 1. Soil nematodes occupy multiple trophic positions and contribute to key processes in soil food webs. Their communities vary across land uses and environmental conditions, yet it remains unclear whether these differences mainly reflect taxon replacement or nested patterns of taxon occurrence. 2. Here, we analysed two independent European datasets of soil nematode communities, SOB4ES, based on eDNA metabarcoding, and NemEu, based on morphological identification, to examine how genus composition varies across land uses. We partitioned community dissimilarity into turnover and nestedness-resultant components and compared sites under contrasting land uses with those sharing the same land use, while accounting for geographical and soil-related variation. We also assessed matrix-level nestedness, differences among trophic groups and associations between genus composition and environmental gradients. 3. In both datasets, genus turnover was consistently greater between contrasting land uses than within the same land use. Although the differences were modest, they remained significant after accounting for geographical distance and genus richness, whereas nestedness-resultant dissimilarity contributed little to land-use differentiation. These findings suggest that land-use-associated differences in European nematode communities are expressed primarily through changes in genus identity rather than nested patterns of taxon occurrence. 4. The consistency of this result across independently assembled datasets supports the broader relevance of taxonomic turnover for understanding soil biodiversity patterns across European land uses.

papers.title: What to Practice Next? Latent Profile-Guided Task Selection for Skill-Evolving LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Task selection shapes the experiences available for skill evolution in LLM agents, yet fixed practice schedules overlook differences in skill requirements and evolving task value. Most existing methods, however, rely on fixed schedules or scalar measures of progress, leaving nonstationary skill demands unaddressed. We propose SPG-Select, a framework for allocating limited practice budget using a multidimensional profile inferred from binary outcomes via MIRT. The framework predicts surrogate progress, defined as the difference between consecutive profile estimates, and prioritizes progress in dimensions with larger estimated proficiency gaps. Our SPG-Select-R policy combines these predictions with uncertainty-based exploration and periodic restarting to accommodate nonstationarity. We evaluate SPG-Select on ALFWorld and WebShop with three skill-evolution backends. In the reported runs, SPG-Select-R achieves higher mean held-out terminal success than uniform sampling in all six backend-benchmark combinations, with gains of 1.49-13.18 percentage points on ALFWorld and 0.93-3.13 points on WebShop. Under a predictable linear surrogate model and boundedness assumptions, we establish a high-probability dynamic pseudo-regret bound for surrogate task allocation in terms of parameter path variation.

papers.title: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space. As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space. Combined with Hassell's theorem, this gives a new proof of scarring in the physical space for almost every stadium. In higher dimensions, we obtain an entropy bound for the ergodic components of such measures. We also construct counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.

papers.title: Foundation Model Fine-Tuning with Attention-based Multi-View Fusion for Multi-Task Cardiac Function Assessment
papers.abstract: In cardio-oncology, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is the standard biomarker for monitoring cardiac function during cancer therapy. However, its estimation from echocardiography is highly operator dependent, and clinically meaningful declines are often detected only after myocardial injury has progressed, motivating automated methods for standardized assessment and earlier detection of LV dysfunction. To address this need, we propose a multi-task framework integrating cardiac cycle-based temporal standardization, multi-view spatiotemporal feature extraction, and joint optimization for LVEF estimation and LV dysfunction classification. Apical four- and two-chamber echocardiographic sequences are temporally standardized by sampling a clip over an estimated cardiac cycle before being processed by the EchoPrime foundation model, which is fine-tuned end-to-end within the proposed architecture. View-specific features are fused through an attention-based aggregation module to generate a patient-level embedding, from which two task-specific prediction heads estimate continuous LVEF and binary LV dysfunction. To broaden the LVEF distribution encountered during training, samples from the MIMIC-IV-ECHO dataset are incorporated using a balanced sampling strategy. Evaluated on the EchoRisk-MICCAI Challenge, our method achieves an MAE of 4.003 for LVEF estimation (Task 1) and an AUC of 0.764 for LV dysfunction detection (Task 2) on the validation set, demonstrating the effectiveness of foundation model fine-tuning with attention-based multi-view fusion for automated cardiac function assessment in cardio-oncology.

papers.title: Trajectory-Based Bayesian Discovery of a Host-Pathogen Model from Quasi-Steady-State Observations
papers.abstract: System identification of nonlinear dynamical systems becomes challenging when the measured data come from a nearly settled state. We study this situation in the case of a bistable host-pathogen interaction model with a cubic term, whose seven true mechanisms are hidden among twenty candidate terms. The data are from one noise-free trajectory on a quasi-steady-state observed window and the initial state. In this situation, classical sparse identification approaches fail to identify the correct mechanisms as the candidate library becomes ill-conditioned along the quasi-steady-state trajectory. To address this, we propose an alternative approach in which sparse Bayesian learning and $\ell_{0}$ iterative hard thresholding with pursuit provide a good start, and a two-swap climb on the Bayesian evidence of the candidate ODE solutions recovers the true model. Our results show successful model recovery, i.e., correct identification of its support and accurate estimation of its coefficients, as validated by exhaustive scoring.

papers.title: Causal Regularization for Robust Prediction
papers.abstract: Prediction is an important use of a statistical model. However, predictive systems typically struggle when the environment, in which they were trained, changes. Robust prediction that can deal with distributional shifts has become an active research area. Existing approaches tend to make strong assumptions in order to achieve prediction guarantees. In this paper, we only require finite second moments in the training data to obtain sharp prediction guarantees. We generalize causal regularization to a framework that uses two environments and measures the differences between them through a generalized risk difference induced by changes in second-order moments of the covariates and response. By defining a sieve of out-of-sample distributions, we derive a worst-risk decomposition over increasing classes of environments and obtain a closed-form estimator that interpolates between OLS and the regularization limit solution. Causal interpretation is recovered under the inner-product invariance condition and when the conditional mean of the target given its causal parents remains invariant across environments. Our results show that the proposed estimator can achieve prediction stability over a broad class of perturbed environments, even when trained on a limited set. The framework separates two goals: robustness as a stable prediction under weak assumptions and causality as a stronger property obtained with additional invariance structure.

papers.title: RescueVLM: Model-Agnostic Vision-Language Framework for Rescue Drone Imagery
papers.abstract: A single unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) mission over an incident site produces hundreds of images, far more than a rescue commander can review under time pressure, and human screening of destruction imagery carries a documented psychological cost. The two obvious remedies both fail in search and rescue (SAR) practice: cloud vision-language model (VLM) services are excluded because the imagery must not leave the incident network under GDPR and German civil-protection (BOS) rules, and fine-tuned specialist detectors age quickly while retraining and re-certifying them exceeds most SAR organizations resources. We present RescueVLM, an open-source, training-free and model-agnostic triage tool built on SketchVLM: a general-purpose open-weight VLM runs fully on-premise and is swapped for a newer model through a simple dropdown selection, so triage quality grows with the underlying models because all task knowledge lives in prompts and an output contract rather than in trained weights. One natural-language query over a mission folder returns a ranked shortlist with per-image justifications, editable SVG overlay annotations, and a GPS map of the hits. In a qualitative evaluation on German fire-brigade field data from three real deployments and a live fire exercise, a single query condenses an entire survey mission into a handful of annotated frames that a commander can review at a glance.

papers.title: Construction and discrete approximation of the renormalized fractional parabolic Anderson model
papers.abstract: For a directed polymer in a discrete fractional Gaussian environment, we identify the scaling limit of its partition field with the renormalized Stratonovich solution of the one-dimensional parabolic Anderson model with fractional noise and flat initial condition. The underlying walk is simple and symmetric, and the temporal and spatial Hurst indices satisfy $H_0>\frac12$, $\frac12\le H_1<1$ and $2H_0+H_1<2$. After an explicit deterministic normalization, the interpolated partition field converges in law in $C_{\rm loc}([0,\infty)\times\R)$, with convergence of all finite moments of its supremum norm on compacts. We construct the limiting field directly by smoothing the noise in the equation and subtracting the corresponding stationary counterterm. The classical solutions converge in $L^p(Ω;C(\mathcal K))$ for every $1\le p<\infty$ and every compact space-time rectangle $\mathcal K$, including those that meet the initial line $t=0$. For $2H_0+H_1>\frac53$, the limit agrees with the solution that Chen, Ouyang, Tindel and the author constructed using regularity structures. The construction also covers the new range $\frac32<2H_0+H_1\le\frac53$. The proofs rely on Feynman-Kac representations and on estimates and invariance principles for weighted self- and mutual intersections of random walks and Brownian motions, together with uniform increment estimates and Gaussian hypercontractivity.

papers.title: CARET: Clinical Assertion-Aware Residual Calibration for Medical Image-Text Alignment
papers.abstract: Medical vision--language models align radiographs with free-text reports, but radiology language distinguishes explicit findings, negation, uncertainty, and omission. Treating these report states as interchangeable during feature adaptation can change image predictions without supporting visual evidence. We introduce CARET, a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that retains pretrained image and text encoders and uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to define a low-dimensional semantic correction space. A bounded residual adjusts image features along these directions, while assertion-aware supervision distinguishes explicitly present and absent findings from uncertain or unmentioned ones. At inference, the adapter requires only an image; textual references remain fixed. In zero-shot classification, CARET achieves 67.80\% accuracy on CheXpert 5$\times$200 and 65.20\% on RSNA. These scores exceed the published CLEFT-LoRA results by 1.06 and 0.27 percentage points, respectively. Comparisons to literature baselines are informative but not controlled for differences in pretraining and evaluation protocols. Ablations across eight components identify the four-state distinction and assertion objective as major contributors, with task-dependent effects for nonmention preservation and pair alignment.

papers.title: The Algebra of Narratives and the Monitoring of Their Relative Dominance
papers.abstract: We propose an algebraic methodology for measuring the relative prevalence of competing narratives within a time-evolving corpus of texts. Standard cosine similarity between article embedding and narrative vectors fails to isolate the idiosyncratic contribution of each narrative, because narratives sharing a common topic produce strongly correlated vector representations. We address this by orthogonalizing the narrative vectors via a global max-min optimization on the Stiefel manifold, which neutralizes shared semantic components while preserving each narrative's specific direction. We ground this geometric procedure in a linear generative model for article embedding that provides an unbiased estimator of narrative prevalence and formally explains why the naive approach suffers from a correlation bias. Empirical validation on the publicly available News Category Dataset (Huff Post, 2012-2018) confirms that the orthogonalized estimator recovers narrative-specific dynamics aligned with known historical events, whereas the naive cosine projection yields synchronized, uninformative time series.

papers.title: LEAP-LLM: Preserving lead-time structure for question-conditioned ECG interpretation
papers.abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) records cardiac electrical activity across multiple leads and is used for detecting cardiac abnormalities. Recent ECG-language models enable large language models (LLMs) to interpret cardiac signals and answer clinically relevant questions. However, existing ECG-language models typically encode the ECG independently of the clinical question, forcing the ECG representation to retain broad and potentially irrelevant signal information. Moreover, these models often aggregate information across leads which can obscure lead-specific details needed for a particular question. To tackle these limitations, we introduce LEAP-LLM, an ECG-LLM architecture for Lead-aware ECG Alignment with Prompt conditioning. LEAP-LLM uses the clinical question to guide ECG feature extraction while preserving explicit lead and temporal structure. Task-trained instruction representations distill information from the question and guide two complementary branches. The Lead branch captures question-relevant temporal patterns within each ECG lead, while the Temporal branch summarizes relevant information across leads at each temporal position. Together, they provide the LLM with compact, question-relevant ECG information while preserving lead and temporal structure. LEAP-LLM reduces modality-token count by 89.0% and prefill FLOPs by 7.2x on average relative to other ECG-LLMs baselines. Across four ECG benchmarks, LEAP-LLM achieves better performance, including a 3.4-percentage-point improvement in G12EC over the strongest prior ECG-specific method. We further show that the model adaptively emphasizes the clinically relevant anatomical lead groups for different cardiac abnormalities, with lead importance patterns consistent with established diagnostic knowledge, providing interpretable evidence that the predictions are supported by clinically meaningful ECG structure.

papers.title: Interaction between fluids and Helfrich membranes
papers.abstract: We propose a finite-element method to determine the dynamics of a fluid interacting with a membrane---a fluid layer equipped with a Helfrich elastic free energy [W. Helfrich, Z. Naturforschung C, 28, 693, (1973)]. Our analysis is based on a partitioned approach, where the state of the fluid, of the membrane, and of the mesh, are solved for at staggered steps. We show the predicting capabilities of the method by considering a macroscopic example of an elastomer membrane, which bulges as it interacts with air injected through a channel. We demonstrate that our method allows for describing large membrane deformations which are not accessible by perturbative methods. We discuss the limitations of our method, by characterizing its added-mass instability. Finally, we show how our analysis allows for understanding the physical mechanism of bulge formation, which is due to a combination of elastic stresses and membrane boundary conditions.

papers.title: Recovered or Memorized? Investigating Dynamical Consistency and Faithfulness in World Model Latents
papers.abstract: World models develop internal simulators that can learn the structure and dynamics of an environment. It has been demonstrated that their internal representations are both meaningful and causal, but are these representations faithful to the governing dynamics of the environment they are learning? We introduce Anchored Recovery Certification (ARC), a procedure that utilizes a discrete Fréchet distance calculation with ground truth to evaluate dynamical consistency on candidate world models up to an affine gauge. We use the procedure on TD-MPC2 (decoder-free world model) that has learned the pendulum swing on an observation lift under varying hyperparameters at k = 5, 10, 25 steps. The model is then steered within a PCA-derived intervention subspace and compared against a ground-truth simulator using relative error to investigate dynamical faithfulness. ARC sufficiency held for TD-MPC2 most consistently at k = 10, with six of seven constraints statistically significant after Holm-Bonferroni correction, while the relative error between the simulator and the causal latent remained substantial. Further research could be conducted with decoder world models such as DreamerV3 (reconstruction loss) to investigate whether the results differ.

papers.title: LEDGER: LLM-Evidence-Driven Graph-Encoded Clustering-Friendly Representations for Short Texts
papers.abstract: Short-text clustering is important for analyzing user-generated content in social networks and online services, supporting applications such as topic discovery and user intent analysis. However, the desired grouping depends on an application-specific clustering criterion that general-purpose text embeddings may not capture. Large language models (LLMs) can apply such a criterion to a pair of texts without human annotation, and existing methods use their responses as generated descriptions, binary decisions or selected neighbours. These discrete outputs discard how strongly the LLM supports a pair and how many judgments stand behind it. Each judgment is also used alone or within the neighbourhood of a single text, so the relations that link judgments across the corpus remain unused. In this paper, we propose LEDGER, an LLM-guided graph representation learning framework for short-text clustering. LEDGER aggregates the repeated numerical scores of each text pair into an accumulated score and an observation count, which define an evidence target for every queried pair. The pairs whose scores reach a threshold form a relation graph, over which a graph encoder propagates text features with a propagation range learned jointly with the encoder. A pairwise predictor trained to match the evidence targets shapes the learned representation, and a distilled student encoder extends it to unqueried texts without further LLM requests. Extensive experiments on seven datasets with four frozen text embeddings show that LEDGER achieves the highest mean clustering accuracy and NMI against five comparison methods, and ablations show that the graph, the learned propagation range and the evidence target each improve performance.

papers.title: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized cone
papers.abstract: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized right circular cone is determined. The field is expressed as the product between the demagnetization tensor describing the geometrical part of the problem and the magnetization. Additionally, its magnetic scalar potential is expressed as the product between a demagnetization vector and the magnetization. All nine components of the tensor and three components of the vector are expressed in terms of elliptic integrals of the first, second and third kind, and a single scalar function of the field point. This function is given as a one-dimensional integral and as a series, and it reduces to the known logarithm on the axis of the cone. The demagnetization tensor and vector for the truncated cone and the annular cone are given by simple superposition. The magnetometric demagnetization tensor is also derived in closed form. The tensors are verified against direct numerical integration of the surface charges and with a finite element model, showing excellent agreement.

papers.title: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized circular piece
papers.abstract: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized circular piece, i.e. the part of a finite cylinder that is cut off by two planes parallel to the coordinate axes, is determined. The field is expressed as the product between the demagnetization tensor describing the geometrical part of the problem and the magnetization. All nine components of the tensor are expressed in closed form in terms of elementary functions and incomplete elliptic integrals of the first, second and third kind. The complementary geometrical piece, bounded by the same arc from the outside, is obtained from the same expressions. The solution, implemented in the open source magnetic framework MagTense, is verified against direct numerical integration and against a finite element calculation of the magnetic field, showing excellent agreement.

papers.title: Clustering-Based Artificial Tree Ensembles for Random Forest Approximation
papers.abstract: Random Forests (RFs) offer strong prediction performance but are difficult to interpret. Most representative trees (MRTs) and artificial representative trees (ARTs) provide surrogate explanations, but a single tree may miss patterns within a forest. We investigate benefits and limitations of clustering-based representative tree ensembles for RF surrogate modeling and assess the contribution of similarity-based clustering relative to random tree partitions. Using linear and nonlinear simulations and regression benchmarks, we evaluate fidelity, prediction accuracy, complexity, and prediction stability against equally sized ensembles of top-ranked MRTs and randomly selected trees. Increasing ensemble size generally improves fidelity, accuracy, and prediction stability. ART ensembles show higher fidelity in simulations and often greater prediction stability for small ensembles. Compared with random tree partitions, similarity-based clustering generally improves ART fidelity in simulations and often on benchmarks. On benchmark datasets, MRT-based ensembles generally achieve higher fidelity and prediction accuracy, whereas ART ensembles have fewer terminal nodes. ART ensembles provide compact surrogates when reduced complexity matters and their fidelity and prediction accuracy meet application requirements. These findings clarify both the trade-offs of representative tree ensembles as RF surrogates and the contribution of similarity-based clustering beyond random clustering.

papers.title: Actuarial-Informed Neural Networks: Constrained Deep Learning for Sex-Specific Multi-Population Longevity Forecasting
papers.abstract: We introduce Actuarial-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a constrained deep learning framework for sex-specific multi-population longevity forecasting that embeds actuarial knowledge into LSTM training through differentiable penalty terms. Applied to a high-longevity 6-country cluster (Switzerland, Sweden, Norway, West Germany, Netherlands, Japan; 1956-2020), the framework is a challenger to the Li-Lee benchmark and unconstrained neural approaches. Our central finding is that monotonicity constraint intensity lambda functions as a continuous governance dial with a quantifiable accuracy-stability trade-off. At lambda = 0.01, 30-year forecast confidence intervals narrow by 6.5% at zero RMSE cost. At lambda = 0.1, they narrow by 25% at only +0.84% RMSE cost. This trade-off is invisible to standard hyperparameter optimizers, which select lambda by minimizing one-step RMSE, the wrong metric for structural constraints in recursive forecasting. The framework adds three contributions: (i) residual-calibrated process noise that eliminates double-counting in the dual uncertainty framework, reducing confidence intervals by 53-60%; (ii) a 5-seed model ensemble with a coefficient of variation of 1.06%; and (iii) a time-varying credibility weight Z(t) = exp(-alpha t) connecting to Buhlmann credibility theory for blending neural and actuarial predictions. A 10-year out-of-sample backtest (trained on 1956-2010, validated against observed HMD life expectancy for 2011-2020) yields a mean absolute error of 0.38 years, with 11 of 12 country x sex combinations within the 90% confidence interval. The model produces regulatory-grade outputs including Solvency Capital Requirements under the Swiss Solvency Test (ES 99.0%: +1.91 years, CHE Male) and Solvency II, reverse stress testing, and model-based stability verification (amplification ratio 1.02x).

papers.title: Accelerating Variational Cone-Beam CT Reconstruction with Learned Warm Starts
papers.abstract: Variational reconstruction provides a rigorous framework for cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) by combining an explicit acquisition model with image priors. However, iterative optimization remains computationally demanding, particularly under severe noise and sparse-view conditions. Although learning-based methods achieve high reconstruction quality, they often replace the original variational formulation with learned optimization schemes or nonlinear equilibrium models. We propose a neural network-guided warm-start framework that accelerates variational reconstruction while preserving its original formulation. Projection data are first reconstructed using the Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) algorithm, and the resulting image is refined by an image-domain neural network. The network output is used solely to initialize the subsequent model-based optimization, leaving the forward model, data-fidelity term, regularization, and optimization scheme unchanged. A pre-regularization step further improves compatibility with the variational priors. Experiments on pelvic CT images from the SynthRAD2025 challenge show a more than threefold reduction in reconstruction time while maintaining comparable image quality.

papers.title: Revisiting the Capacitance of a Hollow Metal Cylinder
papers.abstract: We complete the analysis of the capacitance of a hollow metal cylinder by deriving series representations for different aspect ratios and a practical formula that approximates the capacitance of the tube for any aspect ratio with an error below 1%.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Type-3 New General Relativity on $Λ$CDM Background
papers.abstract: We investigate whether Type-3 New General Relativity can alleviate the cosmic growth tension. On a $Λ$CDM background, we derive the scalar perturbation equations and find the effective gravitational coupling to exceed Newton's constant throughout the parameter range compatible with ghost-free and background-hierarchy conditions. By confronting the theoretical model with growth-rate measurements from major galaxy redshift surveys, including WiggleZ, SDSS-IV eBOSS, BOSS, and VIPERS, we obtain constraints on the effective coupling that are consistent with the $Λ$CDM value. Consequently, the conditions for stability and tension reduction are mutually exclusive.

papers.title: A proof of the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture on entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We complete the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture: among the one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube, differential entropy is maximized precisely in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. Pang proved the conjecture in every dimension at least $150$. We prove the remaining dimensions using polynomial entropy bounds in dimensions three through six and exact certificates for derivatives of the logarithm of the diagonal projection density. The proof uses integer arithmetic and certified one-dimensional integration. We also derive quantitative stability estimates and determine the optimal asymptotic coefficient of a linear stability bound. The source code and the outputs of all finite verifications accompany the paper.

papers.title: A Practitioner's Guide to Materials Theory and Computation in the Age of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Computational modelling has become a cornerstone of materials science, with advances in atomistic simulations, high-throughput computation, and artificial intelligence transforming how materials are understood, discovered, and designed. These developments build upon generations of theoretical innovations that have translated complex mathematical and physical principles into practical predictive tools. However, the growing diversity of computational methods presents challenges for practitioners seeking a coherent understanding of their theoretical foundations. Drawing upon the author's research experience, this monograph provides a practitioner-oriented, pedagogical overview of computational materials science, unified through the concepts of potential-energy landscapes and statistical sampling. It explores how these concepts underpin structural stability, phase behaviour, and electronic and magnetic properties, through a systematic treatment of empirical force fields, density-functional theory, many-body electronic-structure methods, statistical sampling, and property prediction. It further examines high-throughput workflows, materials databases, and the probabilistic foundations of artificial intelligence. Particular emphasis is placed on atomistic representations, graph neural networks, and generative models, highlighting the roles of symmetry, group theory, differential geometry, and stochastic processes in modern materials modelling. By connecting established physical theories with emerging data-driven approaches, this monograph offers a unified perspective on computational materials science and identifies opportunities and challenges toward physics-informed, efficient, and reliable materials discovery.

papers.title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
papers.abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The model chains two Wiener--Hopf problems in different coordinate systems. The first stage solves the duct-radiation problem analytically in axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the Cartesian plate frame. The core physical insight--that the Weyl--Sommerfeld identity provides an exact spectral bridge between these systems--originates entirely with the authors. The heavy algebra of translating between the two spectral representations, together with the associated numerical verification, was carried out with the assistance of a large language model (LLM), under strict human oversight and independent numerical cross-checking. This division of labour enables the LLM to handle tedious symbolic manipulation without compromising rigour. Results are presented for spinning modes radiating from a cylindrical duct with a subsonic jet into a quiescent ambient. The case study demonstrates that, under systematic verification, LLMs can accelerate tedious algebra in theoretical fluid mechanics, contributing a concrete empirical example to the broader discussion on AI's role in theoretical research.

papers.title: Lower Bound of Thermal Conductivity in Graphene
papers.abstract: The intrinsic thermal conductivity ($κ$) of graphene remains highly controversial because of physical and metrological complexities. Although the thermal bridge method enables reliable measurements, sample fabrication remains challenging. Here, we develop a highly efficient patterning and transfer technique to systematically fabricate and characterize suspended bilayer graphene (BLG) thermal bridges with lengths of 1-30 $μ$m. Suspended BLG with unavoidable polymer residues exhibits length-independent thermal conductivity of approximately 570 W/(m K) at room temperature, remaining nearly constant from 250 to 350 K and robust to rigorous surface cleaning and amorphous silicon nitride substrates. Homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations show that amorphous carbon coverage of only approximately 0.01 monolayer is sufficient to suppress out-of-plane flexural acoustic (ZA) phonons. These findings challenge the prevailing view that rigid substrates suppress ZA phonons more strongly than surface contamination and identify a robust lower bound of $κ$ governed by amorphous surface scattering. This lower bound reflects heat conduction in graphene under realistic device conditions and provides a reference for fundamental phonon transport studies and the integration of graphene into thermal management applications in electronic devices and chips.

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).

papers.title: Multimodal Fusion: A Review of Breast Cancer Advanced and Traditional Modalities
papers.abstract: Purpose: Multimodal medical imaging fusion (MMIF) is an increasingly important approach to breast cancer detection (BCD), as different imaging modalities rely on different physical principles and provide complementary information. No single modality can capture all the structural, functional, and biological information needed for accurate diagnosis and characterization. Methods: This review examines more than 15 imaging modalities used in breast cancer detection, including conventional techniques such as mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), as well as emerging approaches such as thermal imaging, photoacoustic imaging, microwave imaging, and multimodal microscopy. Results: Mammography, ultrasound, and MRI remain among the most widely used modalities, providing complementary structural and functional information. Recent AI advances have enabled fusion at the data, feature, and decision levels, with applications in detection, classification, segmentation, prognosis, and personalized cancer management. Multimodal approaches increasingly combine imaging data with clinical, histopathological, and genomic information. However, important challenges remain, including limited availability of large and diverse multimodal datasets, variations in imaging protocols, missing modalities, limited external validation, and the need for interpretable and clinically reliable AI models. Conclusion: MMIF offers promising opportunities to improve breast cancer detection and characterization by combining complementary imaging and non-imaging information.
