Future research should prioritize robust fusion strategies, standardized and diverse datasets, multicenter validation, explainable and privacy-preserving AI, and the integration of imaging with clinical and molecular data to facilitate reliable translation into clinical practice.

papers.title: Hybrid Compression for Memory-Efficient Matrix-Vector Multiplication
papers.abstract: Iterative machine-learning algorithms repeatedly access large real-valued matrices through matrix-vector products, and their performance is limited by memory bandwidth rather than arithmetic throughput. Lossless compression schemes that support computation directly over the compressed data reduce both the data moved and the memory footprint of these workloads. The mm-RePair framework [11] follows this approach by applying the RePair grammar compressor to the Compressed Sparse Row/Value (CSRV) representation of a matrix and performing matrix-vector multiplications directly on the compressed data. Its effectiveness, however, degrades on matrices that are dense or contain many distinct values. In this paper we present a hybrid strategy for the mm-RePair framework that combines grammar and entropy compression. The CSRV sequence is partitioned into a grammar-compressible component, formed by the entries that mm-RePair can compress effectively, and an entropy-compressible component holding the remaining entries, which is encoded with the ans-fold coder [24]. Compression improves further by sorting and delta encoding the entries of each row in the CSRV representation, and by remapping the alphabet to a contiguous range. Experiments on real-valued machine-learning matrices, including word embeddings and transformer hidden states, show that our hybrid strategy is more compact than the original \mmRepair on every input and reduces the peak memory of multiplication, with the largest gains on dense matrices with many distinct values, at competitive multiplication times. It also outperforms the column-reordering variant of \mmRepair on most of the matrices, and combining the two is even more compact on the sparse ones, at the cost of a much longer compression time. Finally, our strategy scales with the number of threads as well as the original \mmRepair does.

papers.title: From Retouched Images to Paired Videos: A Synthetic Benchmark for Face Video Retouching
papers.abstract: Paired unretouched/retouched face videos are costly to produce because professional editing must remain consistent over time, while releasing identifiable face footage raises privacy, consent, and governance concerns. We present DeepVFR, an initial controlled synthetic benchmark-not a new retouching architecture-for paired face video retouching. Starting from paired synthetic DeepFRR images, Wan2.2 generates mild-motion source clips, and backend-specific face transfer constructs synchronized proxy retouching targets, followed by automatic validity screening and manual visual inspection. DeepVFR contains 1,024 pairs of 150-frame clips at 30 fps, evaluated under an identity-disjoint protocol with explicit frame correspondence; release metadata will record the construction route. Within-benchmark baselines, external checkpoints applied to DeepVFR, qualitative analysis, and a 17-participant ranking study establish reference behavior in the controlled domain. The constructed targets exhibit a substantial low-preference tail in the human study. Because both streams inherit synthetic content and the targets additionally inherit commercial-API or face-transfer artifacts, the benchmark neither replaces artist-retouched captured video nor establishes synthetic-to-real generalization. DeepVFR provides a starting point for paired supervision and controlled evaluation. Data, individual study rankings, and training logs will be made publicly available upon acceptance. Broader motion coverage and real-video validation remain future work.

papers.title: Same Evidence, Different Verdicts: Delivery of CT Images and DICOM Metadata Changes VLM Quality-Control Decisions
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are being proposed as automated checks on clinical imaging inputs, where a scan and its DICOM metadata can disagree; a truncated CT series wrongly admitted to volumetric follow-up, such as lung-nodule growth assessment in screening, biases the measurement. A natural safeguard is to let the model judge the image before it sees the metadata. We find this backfires. On 60 NLST chest CT pairs with coverage defects whose ground truth is computed from scan geometry, a false header that Claude Haiku 5.5 resisted when shown with the image (2% of its detections overruled) overturned 91% of them when it arrived after the model's answer (Nemotron-3.5-VL 43% to 100%). With the order reversed, the image overturned 98-100% of the header's errors (Claude models): whichever source came second won. This is not generic sycophancy: a neutral "please confirm" reversed 0 of 1,072 correct refusals, and the effect persisted when the header arrived as a tool result, as in agentic pipelines. One warning sentence cut sequential reversal to at most 9%, and the pattern held on 24 real mismatched pairs. Contributions: (i) evidence that VLM input-check decisions on identical evidence depend on delivery; (ii) a testbed with exact geometric ground truth; (iii) a validation protocol for clinical VLM input checks. Code, prompts and all call logs: https://github.com/nav92061/ct-vlm-delivery-order

papers.title: Personalized and Adaptive Federated Learning for Canine Cardiomegaly Keypoint Prediction
papers.abstract: In the field of medical imaging, limited data and cross-institutional heterogeneity remain major challenges for training robust deep learning models. Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising approach that enables collaborative training across institutions while preserving data privacy by keeping datasets local. In this work, we propose a structure-aware personalized and adaptive federated learning framework, PAFL, for automatic vertebral heart score (VHS) estimation and cardiomegaly classification from canine thoracic X-rays. Our method treats the task as anatomical keypoint prediction followed by geometry-based VHS computation, introducing implicit structural consistency and improving interpretability. To address cross-institutional heterogeneity, we adopt a parameter-decomposed architecture that separates shared feature representations from client-specific adaptation modules. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive, quality-aware aggregation strategy that dynamically weights client contributions based on both dataset size and model quality, thereby enhancing robustness to non-IID data distributions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PAFL framework improves models' predictive performance compared to isolated training and to conventional and existing personalized federated learning (PFL) methods. Our results demonstrate the potential of integrating structure-aware modeling with PFL for reliable and interpretable medical image analysis.

papers.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
papers.abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.

papers.title: The cop number of the flower snarks, and the generalized Petersen graphs with cop number two
papers.abstract: We study two questions of Morris, Runte and Skelton (Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022)) on the game of Cops and Robbers. First, we show that the flower snark $J_n$ has cop number $3$ for every $n\geq 5$, and that $J_3$ has cop number $2$. The upper bound comes from a three-cop strategy, which we call the rolling wall. It works on every connected graph whose vertices can be arranged in a cycle of columns, each dominated by a single vertex. Because only one cop moves on each turn, the same strategy also shows that the lazy cop number of $J_n$ is $3$ for $n\geq 5$. Second, we prove the conjecture of Morris, Runte and Skelton that the only generalized Petersen graphs with cop number $2$ are $\mathrm{GP}(n,1)$ and the four graphs $\mathrm{GP}(6,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(8,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(9,3)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(12,3)$. The new ingredient is an explicit robber strategy showing that two cops do not suffice on $\mathrm{GP}(3k,k)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(4k,k)$ for $k\geq 4$. The theorem on flower snarks and all of the new lower bounds have been formally verified in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

papers.title: RouteDiff: Low-Dose CT Denoising via Fidelity-Refinement Routing and Hypergraph State Regulation
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have become a strong prior for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) restoration. However, existing samplers apply one structure-detail trade-off to the whole image, set the restoration emphasis of each step by the timestep, and derive each next state recursively from the current one, carrying its errors forward. We propose RouteDiff, a state-aware dual-route diffusion framework that routes detail to where it can be trusted, regulates each reverse step by the state it has reached, and re-enters the trajectory from an anchored estimate. Fidelity-Refinement Routing (FRR) equips one shared U-Net with a conservative fidelity route and a detail-oriented refinement route, fuses them pixel-wise with a confidence map, and exposes their disagreement as route evidence. Hypergraph State Regulation (HSR) organizes the current features and this evidence into a state hypergraph, whose soft hyperedges group scattered regions in the same state. Its readout yields an ordered stage judgment that modulates the bottleneck, and its incidence guides feature interaction in the skip connections. Estimate-Anchored Re-entry (EAR) re-projects a route-aware anchor onto the trajectory at a fixed step and hands the new state back to HSR to be judged again. With the ten network evaluations of its baseline, RouteDiff achieves the best peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) on four datasets with inserted, real and simulated noise (40.95 dB and 95.13% on Mayo 2020; 45.18 dB and 97.23% on Mayo 2016). It also generalizes to unseen doses of real scans and yields the highest Dice (80.92%) in downstream segmentation.

papers.title: Setting Optimal Reserve Prices using Fine-Tuned Language Models
papers.abstract: Online auction houses must set reserve prices for highly differentiated products whose unstructured descriptions contain valuable demand information. Existing approaches generally require managers to specify product attributes in advance. We ask whether a language model can instead learn from listing descriptions and historical bids to set item-specific reserve prices before bidding begins. We fine-tune a pretrained text embedding language model using the structural likelihood of auction bids as its training objective. This directs representation learning toward the valuation distribution that determines the reserve decision. We show that consecutive upper bids identify the tail information needed to set an optimal reserve without observing or modeling the number of potential bidders. A split-sample estimator learns the representation on one half of the data and conducts structural estimation and inference conditional on that representation on the other. We apply the method to approximately 65,800 online used-vehicle auctions. With seller values calibrated to match the sale rate among listings, the model implies a counterfactual net increase of $165.8 million, representing a 14.6% increase above the incumbent reserve policy. The framework translates a listing description and a seller's value into an item-specific reserve recommendation without constructing a product taxonomy or requiring a bid history for the item being priced. It provides an approach to adapting language models for operational decisions in marketplaces where products are heterogeneous and demand-relevant information is recorded in text.

papers.title: Stronger-to-weaker gravity in generalized Brans-Dicke cosmology and implications for the Hubble and $S_8$ tensions
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of a Brans--Dicke-type scalar-tensor theory with non-minimal coupling $A(ϕ)=1+c_1ϕ+c_2ϕ^2$ and power-law potentials $V(ϕ)\proptoϕ^{2n}$ ($n=2,3,4$), in which the dynamics of the scalar field yields a time-varying effective gravitational strength $G_{\rm eff}$. The theory is restricted to ghost-free solutions that also satisfy the dominant energy condition, sub-Planckian field ranges, as well as solar-system and big-bang nucleosynthesis bounds, keeping the scalar sector in a well-controlled and motivated regime. When confronting the model with Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernova data with the SH0ES calibration, the preferred scalar field dynamics lowers the sound horizon and raises the Hubble constant to $H_0=71.09\pm0.66\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for $n=3$, which also shows a moderate Bayesian preference over $Λ$CDM ($\ln B=4.55\pm0.44$) under the adopted priors. We show that, within this framework, the early stronger-gravity and late weaker-gravity phases compete for the same coefficients, forcing the latter to have amplitudes bounded by $1-G_{\rm eff}/G \lesssim 10^{-4}$. The data also prefer only brief weaker-gravity excursions after recombination for $n=2$ and $n=3$, lasting less than $0.1$ e-folds, but $n=4$ shows late-time transitions at $z\lesssim 3$ persisting for up to $\sim 1.9$ e-folds. In all cases the weaker-gravity regime is far too shallow to suppress the growth of structure: the $S_8$ parameter is in fact higher than in $Λ$CDM and the preferred cosmologies are of the early-modified-gravity type.

papers.title: Motility-induced phase separation drives aggregation in chemotactic systems
papers.abstract: We present a unified continuum framework that combines chemotactic feedback with motility-induced phase separation (MIPS) to investigate the physical origin of aggregation in self-secreting cell populations. While classical Keller-Segel theory attributes pattern formation to chemotactic instabilities, we show that this mechanism breaks down in systems with proportional density-dependent (autocrine) production and uptake: linear stability analysis reveals that chemical fluctuations decouple from density, eliminating chemotactic aggregation at leading order. In contrast, introducing density-dependent motility restores instability through a purely mechanical mechanism corresponding to MIPS. Our results demonstrate that chemotactic feedback does not alter the nature of this instability, but instead enhances its growth rate and accelerates aggregation. This unifies two central paradigms of biological self-organization and revises the role of chemotaxis in collective cell migration.

papers.title: Relativistic and quantum fluid dynamics: nonlinear momentum evolution
papers.abstract: We present an alternative framework for nonlinear momentum evolution in fluid dynamics, in which relativistic effects are proposed as an underlying mechanism for nonlinear behavior, even in the low-velocity regime. By interpreting the second-order velocity diffusion equation from a quantum-mechanical perspective, we establish a connection between higher-order viscous transport and the reduced Planck constant, identifying the second-order viscosity coefficient with \(\hbar\). Furthermore, we show that the coupling of second-order velocity diffusion and nonlinear momentum evolution leads to a Dirac-type equation for quantum fluids. These findings reveal a potential connection among relativistic effects, higher-order fluid transport, and quantum wave dynamics.

papers.title: How shared pedigrees shape gene genealogies in finite admixed populations
papers.abstract: Gene genealogies along a chromosome are dependent not only because nearby alleles tend to experience no recombination and are therefore inherited together, but also because alleles at different loci may share parental histories through a common ancestor. Disentangling physical linkage and shared parental trajectories is key to understanding how demography shapes genetic diversity. We develop a mathematical framework for describing the joint genealogies of sampled alleles in a finite admixed population, tracing their ancestry backward to the source populations while explicitly accounting for parental relationships and recombination events. Under a Wright--Fisher model, we show that the joint gene genealogy forms an absorbing Markov chain, derive the likelihood of local ancestry, and connect it to other quantities of interest, notably the admixture fraction. We further establish that, once demographic parameters become constant, local ancestry converges to distinct limiting distributions depending on the demographic setting. Under isolation, chromosomes undergo infinitely many recombination events and linkage disequilibrium is due to drift within population replicates, retaining traces of past admixture events. Under constant gene flow from source populations, recent contributions progressively erase the influence of earlier ancestry. Using the joint genealogy of two alleles, we obtain the limiting variance of admixture fractions in both regimes. We illustrate our framework's flexibility through simulations of endogamy and selection. These examples show how genetic diversity depends on the structure of underlying parental relationships. Our work provides a framework for specifying and analyzing complex demographic scenarios and clarifies the links between local ancestry and mating patterns.

papers.title: A Clifford algebra approach to bosonic strings with fermionic boundaries
papers.abstract: The Brauer-Weyl (1935) theorem states that the algebra of tensor products of spinors is isomorphic to the Clifford (geometric) algebra, in any number of spacetime dimensions. The algebraic relation between fermions and bosons seen in the standard model agrees with the Brauer-Weyl theorem, but not with supersymmetry. It is commonly argued that string theory requires supersymmetry, on the grounds that nonsupersymmetric bosonic string theory (1) does not admit fermions, and (2) has an unstable tachyonic ground state. This paper rebuts those standard objections, pointing out that bosonic string theory admits ferm\-ions lying on a D-brane boundary of open strings, and that the open-string tachyon has all the properties of a Higgs field. The original 1970s formulation of bosonic string theory, re-envisaged as a theory of all the forces, not just the strong force, fits the standard model beautifully.

papers.title: Magnon binding in a quantum Hall ferromagnet with a periodic electric field
papers.abstract: A spin wave in a filling-one quantum Hall ferromagnet is neutral but carries an electric dipole perpendicular to its momentum. A spatially periodic electrostatic potential therefore creates parallel channels for spin waves. We use this established mechanism to calculate how confinement changes the exchange binding of magnons travelling in the same direction. Narrower channels increase the overlap of their transverse wavefunctions and strengthen the effective attraction. In an isolated harmonic channel, the energy required to remove one magnon from a cluster of $N$ is $π(k_*\ell)^4N(N-1)/4$ times the transverse level spacing to leading order, where $k_*$ is the mean wave number along the channel and $\ell$ is the magnetic length. We predict the frequency and momentum dependence of the spectral line for adding a second magnon to one already present, both in an isolated channel and in a coupled array. Tunnelling in a wide array can make the binding energy exponentially small, while a strip narrower than the transverse pair size recovers one-dimensional binding at sufficiently weak attraction. We also find that a moving potential can carry a single wave packet with less spreading than free propagation when its initial group velocity matches the potential's speed.

papers.title: Third-Place Solution for the UCF UrbanTwin V2X-Real Track at ECCV 2026: Synthetic Point Cloud Generation and Sim-to-Real 3D Object Detection
papers.abstract: This report presents a complete technical solution for the UrbanTwin V2X-Real Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, covering both synthetic point cloud generation and 3D object detection. For data generation, we adopt per-axis quantile calibration. Public V2X-Real training data are used to construct the real reference distribution, and independent one-dimensional quantile mappings are estimated for the x, y, and z axes of the base synthetic point clouds. The calibrated point clouds are then resampled using a fixed random seed and clipped to the valid spatial range, producing 50 frames with 2,000 float32 XYZ points per frame. For detection, we use a two-stage Voxel R-CNN (VoxelRCNN) detector trained with RangeLDM-enhanced synthetic point-cloud data, point clouds downsampled to 50k points per frame, and reconstructed pedestrian data. Training is performed on four NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPUs with a global batch size of 16 for 40 epochs. Final testing uses direct single-model inference with the original VoxelRCNN model. On the official evaluation server, the normalized Realism score is 0.7905 and the normalized Detection score is 0.5583, with mAP@0.5 of 0.3908, BEV mAP@0.5 of 0.4219, and mAP@0.7 of 0.1047. According to the official weighting rule, the final combined score is 0.6 x 0.5583 + 0.4 x 0.7905 = 0.6512. This report documents the complete implementation details of data construction, model training, inference, submission formatting, and official evaluation.

papers.title: Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
papers.abstract: The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. We identify a second elementary transition---the morphing transition---which has no classical counterpart: all eigenstates hybridize and turn chaotic concurrently, so that no regular subsequence survives at any stage of the crossover. The two transitions are spectrally distinct: the phaseout spectrum is an independent superposition of regular and chaotic subsequences with Berry-Robnik statistics and a finite short-spacing intercept $P(0)$, whereas the morphing spectrum exhibits global level repulsion with Lenz-Haake statistics and $P(0)=0$. We demonstrate both transitions, and their mixture, in three models. The results for the deformed boson model further show that the quantum phaseout scenario is conditional on a smooth quantum-classical correspondence.

papers.title: Determinants of amphichiral knots of braid index at most three
papers.abstract: We show that an odd number n is the determinant of an amphichiral knot of braid index at most three if and only if both n and n + 4 are sums of two squares. The proof rests on the known description of amphichiral knots of braid index three as closures of alternating 3-braid words with a rotation or reflection symmetry (Birman--Menasco, Stoimenov, Jung). Determinant formulas for closed 3-braids are also known (e.g. through the reduced Burau representation at t = -1); what is added here is their evaluation on the two symmetric families, which gives the condition on n + 4, and an explicit construction for the converse. For amphichiral knots of braid index three this describes which determinants occur, which bears on the determinant part of a question of Jung. We did not find the statement in the literature we searched. As a consequence, for an odd n with n + 4 not a sum of two squares, every amphichiral knot with determinant n has braid index at least five; we test this on 4,999 amphichiral knots of Burton's census with up to 19 crossings whose determinant satisfies this hypothesis.

papers.title: Quantum-inspired orthogonal adapters for certifiably robust medical image classification
papers.abstract: Medical image classifiers require not only high accuracy but also reliable predictions under small input perturbations. Certified robustness provides mathematical guarantees of prediction stability, but preserving these guarantees when adapting pretrained models to new tasks remains challenging. We propose a fine-tuning approach based on quantum-inspired orthogonal butterfly layers that preserves the Lipschitz bounds of pretrained certified networks. Inspired by quantum circuits of reconfigurable beam splitters, these layers preserve orthogonality by construction using only $\mathcal{O}(n\log n)$ trainable parameters. Their structured design enables efficient classical implementation and offers a path toward future quantum implementations with logarithmic circuit depth under suitable connectivity assumptions. Controlled experiments on MNIST and MedMNIST demonstrate improved certified robustness compared with conventional alternatives and, in the DermaMNIST transfer, greater resistance to the tested attacks than low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We then apply it to trichoscopic image classification for alopecia diagnosis and alopecia areata activity assessment. By adapting a certified ImageNet-pretrained network, butterfly fine-tuning achieves approximately twice the certified accuracy of conventional fine-tuning and LoRA, with comparable classification accuracy on the same backbone and data split and similar empirical resistance to the tested adversarial attacks. Larger robustness guarantees, including certificates covering certain image-processing transformations, can be obtained at the cost of reduced accuracy. These results highlight the potential of quantum-inspired butterfly layers for parameter-efficient adaptation of medical image classifiers while preserving the mathematical guarantees underlying certified robustness.

papers.title: In-context learning predicts clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms
papers.abstract: Bulk transcriptomes carry information on diagnosis, treatment response and survival, but clinical cohorts are small, and each gets a model of its own that often fails in the next cohort. Here we present PRTS, a 220-million-parameter model that reads a labelled cohort as context and predicts binary, multiclass, continuous or survival endpoints for new samples from whole transcriptomes, without per-cohort training. PRTS was pretrained on 6.0 million tasks generated from public RNA-seq profiles. On 175 held-out tasks and 44 tasks from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), it had the highest mean predictive accuracy, narrowly ahead of TabPFN v3.5, the strongest pre-specified comparator. The lead came from within-cohort prediction and, on TCGA, mainly from survival tasks; across cohorts and at unseen sites, PRTS was level with the strongest tabular models while running more than twice as fast as TabPFN v3.5. The same weights transfer labels to new cohorts from public references, forecast accuracy from pilots, flag suspect labels and attribute predictions to genes. We release the prior, the pretraining code and the model with its weights, together with RealBulk, a collection of 1,160 curated public cohorts, and its benchmark.

papers.title: Amortized conditional inference under changing parameter information in small-angle X-ray scattering
papers.abstract: Many scientific measurements do not uniquely determine the physical system that produced them. Different parameter configurations may explain the same observations, and additional measurements or physical assumptions can change which explanations remain plausible. We develop an amortized conditional inference method to examine these alternatives as the available information changes. Using masked flow matching, the method approximates joint conditional posteriors when different parameters are supplied exactly or with uncertainty. This allows repeated analysis of the same measurement without retraining, while reusing its encoded representation. We can also examine the consequences of assumed parameter distributions and separately assess whether supplied information is compatible with the observation-only posterior. We validate the learned conditionals against analytic posteriors and compare posterior accuracy and inference cost in a simulated scattering benchmark, where the compressed architecture performs better than joint attention on both measures. We apply the method to small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) of cellulose fibrils in paper, examining structural ambiguities in simulated measurements and the effects of physical assumptions on experimental measurements of a paper during hydration. At high humidity, the inferred effective fibril size distribution broadens. Assuming that this distribution remains unchanged instead shifts the posterior towards increased interfibrillar separation, although both interpretations reproduce the measured curves similarly. The compatibility analysis identifies conserved parameter values that are difficult to reconcile with the wettest measurements.

papers.title: Vibe synthesis: hierarchical agentic decision-making for intent-driven multistep molecule synthesis
papers.abstract: The ability to construct complex molecules underpins advances in medicine and the molecular sciences. Yet long-horizon multistep synthesis requires decisions to be revised as evidence accumulates across chemically dependent operations, a capability not readily supported by artificial-intelligence tools and automated platforms organized around predefined tasks and hard-coded workflows. Here we propose and demonstrate a vibe synthesis system (VibeSyn), an intent-driven architecture in which hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined molecular objectives and accumulating evidence into adaptive decisions executed through computational tools and laboratory automation. We evaluate VibeSyn in three demonstrations of increasing scope and autonomy, progressing from evidence-grounded experimental decisions to adaptive execution of a ten-step total synthesis of catharanthine and structure-to-compound synthesis of cyclic peptides containing unnatural amino acids (uAAs). Across the long-horizon campaigns, active human input and simple confirmation account for less than 7.5% and 5.2%, respectively, of recorded workflow actions and outcomes. VibeSyn points towards a future in which chemists define synthetic intent and agent-directed laboratories autonomously navigate the evolving experimental trajectory required to deliver the target compound.

papers.title: Agri-MRAG: Parameter-Enhanced Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Agricultural Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) has shown promise for Agricultural Visual Question Answering (Agri-VQA), but existing methods still face challenges in retrieving relevant knowledge while avoiding redundancy and in integrating retrieved evidence beyond simple prompt concatenation. To address these issues, we propose Agri-MRAG, a multimodal retrieval-augmented framework for agricultural VQA. Specifically, we first introduce a semantic-consistency-guided clustering mechanism that combines multimodal clustering and weighted relevance scoring to select high-confidence knowledge subsets and adaptively determine the retrieval size $k$. We then design a parameterized knowledge injection strategy, where retrieved agricultural knowledge is encoded into LoRA adapters and merged into the feed-forward network (FFN) layers of the MLLM, allowing external knowledge to influence generation through parameter-level adaptation. In addition, a perplexity-guided (PPL-guided) routing mechanism is employed to switch between implicit parametric reasoning and explicit retrieval-assisted generation according to model uncertainty, balancing inference efficiency and answer reliability. For evaluation, we use PlantVillageVQA as a broad agricultural benchmark and construct PlantVQA, a region-specific forestry and fruit crop VQA dataset containing 7,514 images and 15,028 expert-verified question-answer pairs. Experiments show that Agri-MRAG achieves ROUGE-L scores of 41.21 and 46.58 on the two datasets, outperforming mRAG by 11.70 and 4.51 points, and VisRAG by 8.80 and 3.39 points, respectively.

papers.title: AerialOcc: Unified 3D Aerial Perception without Task-Specific Head
papers.abstract: Aerial perception systems are increasingly expected to support diverse tasks, yet existing solutions remain fundamentally tied to task-specific outputs. Detection, segmentation, and other perception objectives are usually learned either by separate models or by sharing a backbone with multiple task heads, leaving the model itself unaware of the common structure underlying these tasks. We are interested in asking: can a single perception representation support different levels of understanding without being designed for any specific task? We notice that occupancy is a promising task-agnostic representation for drone perception. By modeling the spatial existence and semantics of the environment, it naturally bridges different perception granularities, from coarse scene understanding to fine-grained object localization. Therefore, we introduce AerialOcc, a unified occupancy-based perception model that enables multiple drone perception tasks from a single inference process, without maintaining task-specific prediction heads. To facilitate this direction, we construct AerialOcc-20K, a large-scale multi-class occupancy dataset for aerial environments. Extensive experiments show that AerialOcc achieves competitive performance across diverse perception tasks while preserving a unified architecture. Our findings demonstrate that occupancy can serve as a universal perception interface, offering a new perspective toward flexible and scalable visual intelligence for autonomous drones from a common 3D scene representation. Models and data are publicly available at https://github.com/guxiang2002/AerialOcc

papers.title: Gradient-Guided Hardware-Native MIXFP4
papers.abstract: Blackwell tensor cores support native inference with 4-bit weights and activations (W4A4), but NVFP4 leaves a perplexity (PPL) gap to BF16. Choosing a format for each 16-element block can improve accuracy, but current matrix multiply instructions cannot execute choices this fine. Applying these rules at hardware-compatible tiles loses most of their benefit. We introduce FlipQuant, which selects E2M1 or E0M3 for each MMA weight tile. It keeps both quantized weight candidates fixed and learns a binary format map from end-to-end gradients of a bucketed KL loss to a BF16 teacher, re-evaluating them after each update. Native kernels execute 16 x 64 tiles on SM120 and 256 x 64 tiles on SM100 with median GEMM overheads of 1.9% and 1.7%, respectively. Across six language models and two corpora, FlipQuant at 16 x 64 closes 42.5% of NVFP4's PPL gap to BF16 on average, compared with 13.3% for FourOverSix. Code is available at https://github.com/brian030128/flipquant.

papers.title: Can a Vision-Language Model Tune Clustering In Context?
papers.abstract: Clustering is a widely used unsupervised learning method, but selecting an appropriate algorithm and set of hyperparameters for a specific dataset can require many possible configurations and evaluations. In this work, we investigate whether a Vision-Language Model can instead visually evaluate clustering results and use those decisions to then tune an explicit clustering algorithm. We study this through three progressive experiments using Qwen3.5-27B and five controlled synthetic clustering scenarios. First, we test whether the VLM can distinguish the best clustering result from a pair of plots. Second, we test whether it can assign numerical scores to those plots where a higher score represents a better result. Finally, we use these judgments within an agentic loop in which the VLM scores a k-means clustering and proposes updated hyperparameters that may result in better clustering. Our exploratory results show that the VLM performs well when clear cluster structure is present, while struggling on more ambiguous and noisy settings. In the full agentic experiment, the VLM produces clustering configurations with silhouette scores relatively close to those of grid search and Bayesian optimization, while terminating in much fewer iterations. Overall, these results provide an initial proof of concept that VLM-based visual feedback can be used to autonomously tune an explicit clustering algorithm.

papers.title: China's Local Government Debt, Strategic Competition, and Bitcoin Demand: A Conditional Transmission Framework
papers.abstract: How might the resolution of China's local-government debt affect strategic competition and Bitcoin demand? This paper develops a conditional framework connecting debt accounting, bank balance-sheet adjustment, public spending priorities, and constrained portfolio substitution. A debt swap can increase recognized government debt without increasing consolidated principal, while its effect on credit capacity depends on capital relief, loss recognition, and recapitalization. A protected strategic-spending floor can preserve current effort while shifting adjustment toward civilian productive services. In the asset block, stronger relative preference for Bitcoin does not ensure greater effective demand: access constraints and global funding conditions can reverse the sign. We derive a finite-shock threshold and deterministic sign bounds, and distinguish Bitcoin demand from demand for dollar stablecoins. Reproducible numerical illustrations and channel-removal exercises show that opposite outcomes are compatible with the same assumed fiscal stress. The analysis uses dated primary sources to establish institutional context, but estimates neither a debt-to-Bitcoin causal coefficient nor a price-impact scale. Its contribution is a compact set of conditions and measurement distinctions for evaluating transmission claims, rather than an unconditional price forecast or an inference about conflict probabilities.

papers.title: Angel: Anchor-Structured Neural Gaussians for Explicit Fetal Diffusion MRI Slice-to-Volume Reconstruction with Cross-Subject Learning
papers.abstract: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) provides a noninvasive view of developing tissue microstructure and white matter tracts in the fetal brain. During acquisition, however, fetal motion disrupts spatial correspondence between slices, diffusion encoding directions and signal intensities. We introduce ANGEL, an anchor-structured neural Gaussian framework for accurate slice-to-volume reconstruction (SVR) of fetal dMRI, that simultaneously estimates diffusion signal, fetal motion and intensity artefacts. Unlike standard explicit Gaussian representation, ANGEL is designed to prevent absorption of noise and artefacts into the reconstructed dMRI by learning a compact representation of spatio-angular signal via a shared decoder that predicts 3D Gaussians across anchors and subjects. The individual anatomical variability is compactly represented through subject-specific anchors. Experiments on simulated neonatal and in vivo fetal data show significant improvement of dMRI reconstruction in both spatial and angular domains, in comparison to explicit Gaussian representation, implicit neural representation as well as classical methods.

papers.title: Mutual Colormap Dependence: How Recoloring Biomedical Images Changes Vision-Language Model Answers
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are being built to answer questions about biomedical images, yet they never see the measured intensities, only the colors that a colormap has assigned to them. For questions about image content, the colormap should not change the answer. We call the extent to which it does Mutual Colormap Dependence (MCD), the mutual information between the colormap and a model's answer, which is zero exactly when every colormap yields the same answer distribution. Because VLMs sample their answers, we compare recoloring with a control that uses the same number of calls to ask again about the unchanged gray image, so that ordinary resampling is not mistaken for an effect of the colormap. We test GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Qwen3-VL-235B under six luminance-monotonic colormaps (gray, viridis, plasma, inferno, magma, and cividis) on 50 medical visual-question-answering items from 16 SLAKE images, 64 ChestX-ray14 chest radiographs, and 200 BBBC039 fluorescence-microscopy images for exact nucleus counting. Every prompt tells the model to ignore the colormap. Even so, with three answers per colormap on the chest radiographs, the answers of all four models depend on the colormap (all Holm-adjusted $p \leq 0.002$). For Claude, some colored map overturns the majority answer on 29 of the 64 radiographs, where resampling gray alone overturns about 4, and Qwen's accuracy falls from 0.54 under gray to between 0.32 and 0.41 under the colored maps, mostly because it abstains. With one answer per colormap, recoloring adds disagreement beyond repeated sampling in 5 of 12 model-panel cells under per-cell 95% intervals, and repeating the instruction to ignore color does not reliably reduce it. The colormap is therefore part of what a VLM sees, and it can change the answer.

papers.title: An ODE to Changing Variables: $v = y/x$ Is For Victory
papers.abstract: Most first courses in differential equations introduce students to very special differential equations which can be solved in closed form from a small set of techniques (such as separable equations and integrating factors). Frequently other equations can be converted to one of these forms through a change of variable; however, these transformations are usually just given without any explanation of \emph{how} people found them, or \emph{why} problems of these forms have nice solutions, but not related ones. We consider the first order differential equation $dy/dx = f(x,y)$ where $f(x,y)$ does not factor as $A(x)B(y)$, and assume $f(x,y) = g(y/x^r)$ for some nice function $g$ and some real number $r$. This can be reduced to a separable equation only when $r=1$. We then discuss generalizations and what conditions on $f$ lead to a change of variables yielding a separable equation. Our goals are twofold. First, to encourage students and instructors to be active, questioning the methods and results, seeing how far they can be extended and why they work. Second, we discuss how to appropriately use AI to take ideas and special cases as prompts and quickly create extensions and editable notes that can be shared with students, freeing up professors (and students) from straightforward calculations \emph{without} sacrificing learning and understanding.

papers.title: A multi-fidelity dataset of two-dimensional steady laminar channel flow around obstacles
papers.abstract: Surrogates that correct inexpensive flow simulations need the same flows solved at several fidelities and an estimate of the numerical error of the reference solutions. This dataset contains 4,500 two-dimensional, steady, laminar channel flows past a single obstacle. Each is solved in five numerical configurations: second-order convection on meshes with cell sizes of 2, 1, 0.5 and 0.25 mm, and first-order convection on the 1 mm mesh. A seeded generator draws the obstacles from five shape families in three size classes. All 22,500 OpenFOAM runs were iterated to initial residuals of $10^{-6}$, and each run's residuals, iterations and provenance are recorded. Every run provides the velocity and pressure on a regular grid with geometry channels, and the pressure and wall shear along the obstacle. Its 20 flow attributes, computed on the simulation mesh, include drag and lift split into pressure and friction parts. The four second-order levels give an estimate of the discretisation uncertainty of 19 attributes of every case. Fixed splits include three out-of-distribution test sets.

papers.title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
papers.abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

papers.title: Frame First, Decode Once: Object-Centric Coordinates and Single-Pass Decoding for System-1 World Models
papers.abstract: Single-pass primitive decoders such as LocateAnything and VFlash predict all quantized coordinate tokens of a geometric primitive in one forward pass, enabling fast, System-1 visual planning. We study what matters when such a decoder serves as a System-1 world model: a fast action-conditioned predictor that ranks candidate pushes by their predicted outcome. On ManiSkill3 PushT-v1 (512 held-out test families, 8,192 rollouts) and on human demonstrations from lerobot/pusht (2,384 test windows), we compare decoders, training losses, rigid-body projections and coordinate frames, using matched checkpoints, hierarchical bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm correction. Two factors of similar size dominate. First, expressing inputs and outputs in the SE(2) frame of the object's initial pose lowers decision regret by 1.9-2.2x for each of five decoders, and the object-frame model trained on 128 families matches the world-frame model trained on 512. Second, single-pass decoding outperforms iterative decoding: in the object frame, single-pass heads reach 0.020-0.021 regret at 1.6-1.8 ms per decision, against 0.046 for 10-step DDIM diffusion and 0.059 for KV-cached autoregression at 10.3 and 12.9 ms. The choice among single-pass heads has no measurable effect on regret, and our registered hypothesis that the frame effect exceeds the decoder spread is not supported. Soft-token expectation with an end-to-end 2D Kabsch projection gives the lowest trajectory error (11.35 px on ManiSkill3, 3.78 px on lerobot/pusht), exact rigid-body consistency, and lower regret than diffusion at every budget from 4 to 50 DDIM steps, at 3-29x lower latency.

papers.title: Information about Optic Nerve Head Biomechanics is Already Coded in Your Clinical Charts and Can be Used to Predict Glaucoma Progression
papers.abstract: Glaucoma patients routinely undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging and intraocular pressure (IOP) assessment as part of standard care. Because IOP typically differs across visits, it is possible to map visit-to-visit ONH strains by registering OCT volumes acquired under different IOPs. These strains reflect ONH elasticity and, over longer intervals, also capture growth and remodeling of the ONH. In this study, we evaluated whether such visit-to-visit ONH strain signatures could serve as predictors of glaucoma progression. We retrospectively analyzed 525 eyes from 430 glaucoma patients (238 fast and 287 slow progressors), defining fast progression by a visual field index slope of -1.5% per year or worse. 3D strain maps were derived from baseline and follow-up OCT scans using AI. Predictions using T=1 to T=4 follow-up visits were evaluated by five-fold cross-validation in a long-term cohort (T=1: 1.30 years; T=4: 5.26 years) and short-term testing (T=1: 0.46 years; T=4: 1.25 years). Overall, IOP differed between paired visits in 92% of cases. Long-term T=1 prediction achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.74 and accuracy of 0.72. A single short-term follow-up (T=1) yielded an AUC of 0.75 and accuracy of 0.71; four follow-ups yielded an AUC of 0.87 and accuracy of 0.82. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified neuroretinal rim compression and prelaminar elongation associated with fast progression, with substantial inter-eye variability. Overall, visit-to-visit ONH strains derived from routine OCT predicted glaucoma progression after a single follow-up visit at a mean interval of 0.46 years. These findings suggest that short-term OCT/IOP assessments could provide valuable insights into ONH biomechanics, identify eyes at risk of rapid progression, and reveal distinct strain signatures associated with disease progression.

papers.title: Portfolio-Size Constraints on Default Correlation: Exact Coherence Tests and Sharp Asymptotic Bounds
papers.abstract: An absorbing default process imposes joint restrictions on cumulative default distributions across horizons. We characterize these restrictions for finite homogeneous portfolios. For binomial mixtures whose mixing distribution functions cross at most once, stochastic ordering of the entire default count is equivalent to two inequalities: the probability of no defaults must be nonincreasing and the probability of all defaults must be nondecreasing. In the one-factor Gaussian model, these inequalities give an exact interval of admissible later correlations, obtained from two scalar equations. The intervals are nested as portfolio size increases. If the earlier and later default probabilities are $p_0<p_1$ and the earlier latent correlation is $ρ_0\in(0,1)$, both interval boundaries approach $ρ_0$ at rate $(\log n)^{-1/2}$, with common leading magnitude $ρ_0\sqrt{2(1-ρ_0)}[Φ^{-1}(p_1)-Φ^{-1}(p_0)]$. We also give a constructive absorbing coupling, an exact sequential repair, differential conditions for smooth horizon curves, and a finite-size certificate of incompatibility. Log-domain quadrature, bracketed root finding, and deterministic numerical experiments evaluate the intervals and verify the restrictions on the full count distribution. The framework provides a feasibility analysis of prescribed horizon laws.

papers.title: A Beginner's Guide to Physical Networks
papers.abstract: Network theory studies entities (nodes) and the relationships between them (edges). While these entities and their relationships may be abstract in general, this tutorial focuses on the special case of physical networks: spatially embedded networks that carry physical quantities such as electric charge, fluid volume, or momentum. The underlying structure is described mathematically by a graph (Section I), with the incidence matrix playing a central role in the analysis. Viewing a graph as a special case of a cell complex reveals the topological structure of the incidence matrix and its relation to familiar operators from calculus (Section II). Because these networks are physical, flows are conserved at each node and often derive from the gradient of a potential. Models that satisfy these principles behave analogously to circuits; accordingly, we first review circuit theory (Section III), then examine related fluid flow (Section IV) and mechanical (Section V) networks. Briefly, the topics of random walkers (Section VI) and nonlinear networks (Section VII) will be discussed, followed by concluding remarks (Section VIII). Analytical examples and Python implementations, in lieu of pseudocode, are included throughout. Exercises are included as footnotes. This tutorial is based on a short course taught at the Boulder School for Condensed Matter in 2019 and a course taught at the University of Pennsylvania in Spring 2024. It should be a useful resource for students, teachers, and researchers applying graph theory to physical networks. Knowledge of linear algebra is assumed, but no prior knowledge of graph theory or physics is necessary.

papers.title: Hybrid quantum learning for imbalanced blood-cell classification: domain adaptation and classifier design
papers.abstract: Limited annotated data, class imbalance, and morphological similarity make white blood cell classification challenging. We benchmark hybrid variational quantum classifier heads against an affine baseline on 821 microscopy images across seven morphological classes. Using ImageNet-initialised ResNet34 backbones and repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation, we first compare direct transfer with intermediate adaptation on MLL23, a larger peripheral blood cell microscopy dataset. To guide the head comparison, we explore different encoding strategies, variational depth, and the number of independent circuit blocks. We then compare the classifier performance using the affine head and two hybrid heads across multiple random seeds, under a shared training and evaluation protocol. For this comparison, all backbones share the same MLL23-adapted initialisation. Intermediate adaptation increases mean macro-F1 across all four affine-head fine-tuning configurations. The largest gain occurs with a frozen backbone, where macro-F1 rises from $0.685$ to $0.786$, a relative improvement of approximately $14.7\%$. The shallow two-block hybrid head achieves a mean pooled out-of-fold macro-F1 of $0.865 \pm 0.010$, compared with $0.879 \pm 0.008$ for the affine head. The corresponding balanced accuracies are $0.886 \pm 0.008$ and $0.889 \pm 0.010$, respectively. In the architectural exploration, the two-block hybrid head achieves the highest macro-F1 and balanced accuracy among the evaluated hybrid configurations, while the effect of encoding varies across the considered metrics. Our results help guide the design and evaluation of hybrid classifier heads for imbalanced microscopy by linking architectural choices to overall performance and class-specific precision-recall trade-offs.

papers.title: ST-Dist: Distilling Spatial Transcriptomics Predictions into Interpretable Gene Axes for Distant Metastasis Prediction
papers.abstract: Distant metastasis at diagnosis determines the treatment of prostate cancer, but predicting it from routine biopsy slides is challenging as the signs of metastasis are not clearly localized and are more subtle than in standard tumor detection and subtyping tasks. Multiple instance learning (MIL) on pathology foundation-model features has become the standard approach when labeled data are abundant, but such models remain hard to interpret. Distant metastasis is further challenging, because confirming the label requires clinical follow-up beyond the routine H&E slides. To this end, we propose ST-Dist, which distills the gene expression predicted by a spatial transcriptomics (ST) model into a linear head mapping each tile's foundation-model features onto named gene axes. The slide's projections along these interpretable gene axes are then used for distant metastasis prediction with a simple logistic regression. On 497 prostate needle biopsies (205 patients), ST-Dist reaches an AUROC of 91.37%, above nine MIL baselines. It remains competitive on the public TCGA-COAD and TCGA-KIRC cohorts, and it has the highest mean AUROC over the three cohorts. The ablations on the prostate biopsies show that the gene axes outperform a linear probe on encoder features, dimension-matched principal components, random gene panels and the ST model's own predicted expression, and the gain over the probe holds on all 13 pathology encoder settings that we tested. ST-Dist thus offers a simple, accurate and interpretable route from H&E to distant metastasis prediction.

papers.title: Directional gate-error asymmetry and universal selectivity bounds in non-unital open quantum systems
papers.abstract: Clifford randomized benchmarking and average gate fidelity assign a single trajectory-independent decay rate to a noisy quantum gate at leading order in the dimensionless damping exposure \varepsilon = γT, concealing state-dependent transition-error asymmetries in untwirled quantum circuits. While state-dependent amplitude-damping errors are well known in open quantum systems, a trajectory-level analytical framework that bounds directional transition selectivity across arbitrary pulse shapes and Markovian environments has been lacking. Using first-order toggling-frame perturbation theory for a two-level qubit coupled to a Markovian bath, we show that the antipodal survival-error slopes χ_+ and χ_- along any piecewise-continuous control path depend exclusively on its time-averaged Bloch vector m and transverse residence covariance matrix G, obeying the complete-positivity cofactor bound β(r) \le 1. On a standard polar \sqrt{X} gate, longitudinal T_1 relaxation induces a 12.23 : 1 directional survival-error split (κ_{T_1} = (3π- 8)/(3π+ 8) \approx 0.081767), whereas time-symmetric X rotations maintain an exact 1 : 1 balance (κ_{T_1} = 1). Across all completely positive Markovian generators, coupling between non-unital drift and unital diffusion enforces a selectivity bound κ_\star = (π- 2\sqrt{2})/(π+ 2\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.052456 (19.06 : 1) for time-independent single-qubit πswaps. We apply this framework to Gaussian and derivative-removal-by-adiabatic-gate (DRAG) waveforms on superconducting transmons and trapped-ion qubits, extend the analysis to finite damping, pulse dwell, colored thermal baths, and qutrit leakage, and construct two-branch differential lock-in protocols that isolate directional error splits immune to first-order state-preparation and measurement errors.

papers.title: KernelArmor: End-to-End Agentic System for Establishing Memory and Thread Safety for CUDA
papers.abstract: Optimized CUDA kernels can pass testing while retaining subtle memory and concurrency bugs. We present KernelArmor, an agentic framework that combines LLM-generated annotations with an extended SMT verifier to establish memory and thread safety under explicit contracts. KernelArmor can reason about kernels with advanced CUDA features, such as tensor cores, packed accesses, warp synchronization, asynchronous copies, and library calls, returning source-level diagnostics to guide verification and repair. Across 740 instances containing 1,370 production-grade CUDA kernels, it reports potential bugs in 78.6% of instances and establishes safety for 11.4%, outperforming the evaluated state-of-the-art tools in detection coverage, identifying 100% of cuCatch memory-safety bugs and all in-scope cuHadron races. Integrated into an agentic optimization loop, KernelArmor produces verified kernels in all 77 trajectories while retaining 99% of the unconstrained geometric-mean speedup.

papers.title: Conv-Reluplex: A Verification Framework For Convolution Neural Networks
papers.abstract: In recent years, machine learning has demonstrated impressive performance in many real-world tasks, especially in computer vision and natural language processing. However, to apply them in safety-critical systems one needs formal guarantees on the neural network outputs. The Reluplex tool is proposed to verify the safety of deep neural networks (DNNs), and in case the DNN fails to give a correct output, can generate adversarial examples. Since the tool can only handle DNNs, it is necessary to extend the tool to process image data. Therefore, in this paper, we propose the Conv-Reluplex framework, which is designed to verify the convolutional layer and pooling layer in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and generate adversarial examples when classification is misguided. We conduct several experiments on MNIST to evaluate our approaches. The results show that the original CNN is improved using the adversarial examples generated by our tool, and the precision of classification can be increased significantly.

papers.title: Lower semicontinuity of dimension for quasi-Bernoulli measures under conformal projections
papers.abstract: We study the dependence of the Hausdorff dimension of projected quasi-Bernoulli measures on a conformal iterated function system on the real line. For every fixed quasi-Bernoulli probability measure on the symbolic space, we prove that the dimension of its push-forward under the coding map is lower semicontinuous in the $C^{1+θ}$ topology, without any separation assumption or shift-invariance requirement on the symbolic measure. The proof combines bounded distortion and finite-scale entropy estimates with uniform control of the entropy dimension over measures whose densities are bounded above and below. For invariant Gibbs measures associated with Hölder continuous potentials, we also prove joint lower semicontinuity with respect to the defining system and the potential. As an application, we obtain a generic dimension formula: for each fixed shift-invariant quasi-Bernoulli measure, a dense $G_δ$ set of systems with derivative moduli strictly less than 1/2 has projected dimension equal to the minimum of one and the entropy-to-Lyapunov-exponent ratio.

papers.title: From Hosted Service to Field-Owned Infrastructure: Open, Self-Hosted Real-Time Camera-Trap Alerting with Regional Open-Weight Models
papers.abstract: Cellular camera traps can alert field teams within minutes, supporting anti-poaching, threatened-species protection and human-wildlife conflict mitigation. Most systems use central servers, sending images of people and sensitive species locations outside the collecting organisation and often across national borders. We ask whether this capability can run on infrastructure owned by field organisations. Trap Tracker RT is an open-source, self-hosted application that receives images by email or locally via FTP/SFTP, classifies them with a project-specific model and sends alerts through a mail server chosen by the organisation. We evaluated DeepFaune-SSA v1.2, pairing MegaDetector v6 with a DINOv3-based classifier for 33 sub-Saharan taxa, against three open alternatives on 31,131 out-of-distribution images from Kenya, Namibia and Malawi, independent of its training data. DeepFaune-SSA achieved image-level species accuracy of 0.901 (95% CI 0.894-0.908), versus 0.530 for the global SpeciesNet classifier and 0.556 and 0.547 for YOLOv10x and YOLO26x detectors trained on the same regional data. DeepFaune-SSA had the highest recall for all 26 species evaluated. The single-stage detectors missed animals in about a quarter of images; SpeciesNet assigned species labels in only 57%, usually falling back to coarser labels otherwise. In bench tests of the fully local path, alerts were issued about 6 s after upload completion, including with slowed and interrupted uploads. The two-stage pipeline processed 19 images per minute on eight CPU threads without a graphics processor. Trap Tracker RT is used by five organisations in the United Kingdom and Kenya, including for human-elephant conflict mitigation. We discuss how data paths, rather than inference location, determine data sovereignty, the responsibilities of self-hosting and the ethics of real-time monitoring.

papers.title: Feature-Space Latent Forecasting for Endoscopic Surgical Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Surgical workflow assistance is inherently anticipatory: systems must reason about how procedures evolve, not just recognize the current frame. However, many prior approaches perform prediction in pixel space by synthesizing future frames, which primarily focuses on appearance fidelity rather than the semantic representations required for downstream reasoning. To address this limitation, we propose a feature-space semantic forecasting framework that models temporal dynamics directly within the representations of a frozen Vision Foundation Model (VFM). Specifically, we build a hierarchical target representation from multi-layer VFM features, replace future-frame feature tokens with learnable \texttt{[MASK]} tokens, and train a masked transformer to forecast the corresponding future latent features from observed context, thereby formulating procedural evolution as masked future feature prediction. Experiments on public laparoscopic benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements in phase anticipation, multi-label tool presence prediction, and remaining-time estimation over RGB-based forecasting baselines, while enabling a plug-and-play representation interface for lightweight downstream heads.

papers.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. III. Atomistic condensed-phase simulations
papers.abstract: Accurately accounting for nuclear quantum effects (NQEs), including zero-point energy and nuclear tunneling, is essential for a reliable prediction of the structural, thermodynamic, and dynamical properties of chemical systems, particularly those involving light atoms. However, incorporating NQEs could render simulations of large-scale chemical systems computationally prohibitive, particularly when combined with expensive electronic-structure calculations. One potential avenue for reducing cost is to use bead-Fourier path integrals (BF-PIs). In Paper I, we introduced the BF centroid molecular dynamics (BF-CMD) method, in which BF-PIs were used to compute an effective potential for CMD, and in Paper II, we introduced BF ring polymer MD (BF-RPMD), taking the BF-PI and using it for approximate real-time dynamics. Both papers featured a series of model systems and were able to reduce the number of beads needed to converge dynamical properties by a factor of 2 to 4, depending on the system. In this work, we report the first implementation and application of the BF-PI framework to atomistic simulations using liquid bulk water and hexagonal ice as test cases. As in our previous papers, we find that adding just a single Fourier component to the path yields a 4- and 8-fold reduction in the number of beads while achieving results that agree with reference PI simulations for liquid water and ice, respectively. We also demonstrate that we can reduce simulation costs by up to 5.5x compared to standard PIs by reducing the number of force calculations and normal-mode transformations.

papers.title: Dissipative many-body theory of electron-phonon-photon systems
papers.abstract: Optical cavities offer opportunities to control quantum materials, but radiative leakage and vibrational relaxation call for microscopic theories that treat interactions and dissipation on equal footing. We develop a Keldysh-Lindblad nonequilibrium Green's function framework for interacting electrons coupled to quantized photon and phonon fields. The formulation accommodates boson-number-nonconserving Hamiltonians and dissipative channels that combine electronic transitions with bosonic processes. We derive the mixed electron-boson diagrammatic expansion and the corresponding Kadanoff-Baym equations, retaining environmental noise, initial correlations, and interaction-induced memory. The equal-time equations govern the electronic density matrix and the bosonic covariance. As an illustration, we construct jump operators that preserve a semiconductor with filled valence bands and an empty photon field. Within a mean-field treatment, this state remains stationary although its two-time propagators exhibit dissipative broadening. The framework opens new avenues for studying correlated dynamics in lossy cavities and vibrational environments.

papers.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress by rewatching its execution as video. We instantiate VEX with video-SALMONN-VEX, a 9B-scale audio-visual computer-use agent built on the video-SALMONN 2 architecture with a Qwen3.5-9B backbone. We further introduce Action-Grounded Guide Optimization (AGGO), a reinforcement learning method that optimizes video-derived guidance for downstream action prediction, and augment AgentNet, OSWorld, and CUA-Gym with over 24K real-world tutorial videos. Experiments on OSWorld and a complementary subset of CUA-Gym demonstrate consistent improvements, with video-SALMONN-VEX achieving a 22% relative increase in task success over its Qwen3.5 backbone on OSWorld. Moreover, its generated guidance improves Gemini-3.5-flash by 10% relatively on OSWorld. These results highlight the potential of audio-visual understanding as a unified interface for procedural learning and self-verification in computer-use agents.

papers.title: VTG-RAG: Long-Video Reasoning via Query-Adaptive Coarse-to-Fine Sampling and Temporal Graph Retrieval
papers.abstract: Long-video reasoning requires a system to localize sparse evidence over extended temporal sequences, preserve temporal structure, and generate answers despite substantial multimodal distractors. Existing video retrieval-augmented generation methods typically build indexes from uniformly sampled video segments. In long-video settings, this design readily introduces irrelevant context and is unreliable for questions with explicit temporal constraints. We propose VTG-RAG, a framework for long-video question answering that combines query-adaptive coarse-to-fine sampling with temporal graph retrieval. First, a two-stage sampling strategy selects core segments with high mean query relevance or high intra-segment relevance variance. The framework then integrates subtitles, speech transcripts, visual descriptions, entities, and relations from these segments into a temporally ordered multimodal graph. Finally, it performs temporally filtered, two-pass retrieval and reasoning across frame, text, and graph evidence spaces. A lot of experiments have proven the effectiveness of the VTG-RAG. Specifically, we evaluate the framework on Video-MME and LongVideoBench. On LongVideoBench, the reported Qwen2.5-VL-32B and 72B results improve from 48.16% to 50.56% and from 52.13% to 53.32%, respectively, with 24 answer-input frames. These correspond to gains of 2.40 and 1.19 percentage points. The ablation experiments of VTG-RAG further support that the contributions of each component are very important.

papers.title: Rank-One Sutured Instanton Homology Detects Homology Products
papers.abstract: We prove that a balanced sutured manifold $(M,γ)$ satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C} SHI(M,γ)=1$ is an integral homology product; that is, $H_*(M,R_-(γ);\mathbb Z)=H_*(M,R_+(γ);\mathbb Z)=0$. Consequently, for every taut balanced sutured manifold $(M,γ)$, $SHI(M,γ)\cong\mathbb C$ if and only if $(M,γ)$ is a product sutured manifold. The proof uses the enhanced Euler characteristic of $SHI$ and a specialization formula for sutured torsion.

papers.title: Neural Latent Gaussian Process for 3D reconstruction of Mouse Brain Lipids
papers.abstract: We address the problem of reconstructing continuous three-dimensional lipid profiles of the mouse brain from lipid measurements acquired only on a sparse set of two-dimensional tissue sections. Using MALDI-MSI measurements from coronal sections of two densely sampled and six sparsely sampled mouse brains, registered to the Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework (CCF), we seek to interpolate the measured hundreds of lipid profiles across the unobserved voxels of the reference brain. We introduce a Neural Latent-Space Gaussian Process (LGP) architecture for this task and critically evaluate its ability to reconstruct spatial lipid distributions, using held-out mouse brain sections to assess generalization. We propose a Gaussian Process prior for the distribution of low-dimensional lipid profiles across the mouse brain (with Matérn or a Riemann manifold kernel). This allows us to encode 3D coordinates in a small number of latent 3D volumes that are then mapped to particular lipids using a multilayer perceptron (MLP). We performed an exhaustive analysis over a range of algorithms from simple linear regression, XGBoost, MLP to state of the art models such as Neural Transcriptomic Field, graph-based SPA3D for spatial omics reconstruction and DEEPSPATIAL. We additionally evaluate GPLFR as an alternative Gaussian-process-based approach. Across 173 measured lipids, LGP outperforms all evaluated baselines, including recent spatial-omics models and GPLFR, achieving a mean correlation of 0.613 and demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach for sparse 3D lipid interpolation.

papers.title: Recognizing Events Is Not Enough: Why Streaming VLMs Struggle in Compositional Instruction Triggering
papers.abstract: Recognizing individual events does not guarantee correct execution of compositional instructions in streaming video. For example, given the request "Notify me when the pot boils after someone turns on the stove and leaves the kitchen", existing models may recognize the individual events yet notify too early or miss the intended moment, failing to track how their temporal conditions are satisfied over time. To evaluate this gap, we introduce CoTriggerBench, which composes annotated video events into temporally constrained instructions and verifies notification timing and silence through executable event plans and source-event replay. To address this challenge, we propose a real-time VLM agent, TEMPI. TEMPI decomposes instructions into atomic event queries and temporal constraints, and uses Scenario Memory to continuously maintain task progress as event evidence arrives, allowing earlier observations to support subsequent decisions beyond the detector's visual window. Even when no notification is required, relevant events continue to update the scenario state. On CoTriggerBench, TEMPI achieves 44.4% instruction-level success, outperforming the strongest closed-source and fine-tuned open-source VLM baselines by 15.6 (Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash-Realtime) and 18.1 (MOSS-VL-Realtime) percentage points, respectively. To support efficient on-device streaming inference, we further optimize the streaming inference pipeline by overlapping partial visual encoding and LLM prefix prefill with frame arrival. On an 8 GB RTX 5060, our optimized detector implementation achieves a 4.90$\times$ speedup.

papers.title: Minimality of the Double Kite among Strict Two-Pole Configurations of Unit Triangles
papers.abstract: A strict unit-triangle configuration is a finite connected family of closed equilateral unit triangles in which distinct triangles are disjoint or meet at a common vertex, and no vertex belongs to more than two triangles. A vertex belonging to exactly one triangle is a pole. We prove that every strict configuration with one or two poles contains at least fourteen triangles, a sharp bound for two poles attained by the double kite and the reverse double kite. A strict four-regular configuration whose contact graph has an edge cut of size at most two contains at least twenty-eight triangles. A decomposition into three strict two-pole components requires forty-two triangles; both known ring constructions attain the bound. The proof reduces minimal counterexamples to two-connected contact graphs, applies area bounds to complementary unit-sided polygons, and excludes the remaining cases by exact angle certificates. The supplement contains 13,668 stored marked records, 233 exclusion certificates, a standard-library verifier, and independent checks of the complete enumeration.

papers.title: Target-Free Autocalibration of Stereo PIV Camera Systems via Persistent-State Motion Representations
papers.abstract: Stereo Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) recovers three-component velocity fields by triangulating tracer particles observed by synchronized cameras. It requires an accurate extrinsic calibration, which is still obtained by inserting a physical target into the flow and must be repeated whenever the rig is moved. We present a target-free method that calibrates a stereo PIV rig directly from particle image sequences. Because tracer particles are visually indistinguishable, we match motion rather than appearance: building on CUT3R, each camera stream is processed by a recurrent transformer whose persistent state accumulates particle motion over time. The state is decoded into per-camera optical flow and queried by a cross-view decoder that regresses bidirectional point correspondences, from which the relative pose is recovered with a five-point RANSAC solver. We train on a new synthetic stereo PIV dataset with ground-truth poses and evaluate on standard PIV optical flow benchmarks and on 200 real rig placements. Our model achieves lower flow error than existing PIV networks, more accurate cross-view correspondences than COTR, and higher pose accuracy than the strongest detector-matcher pipelines on both synthetic and real data, without any calibration target.

papers.title: TyphoonWorld: A Residual Token World Model for Probabilistic Forecasting of Typhoon Imagery
papers.abstract: A satellite forecast of a typhoon should give a low-error picture of the next two days, together with an ensemble whose members are coherent fields and whose spread responds to the storm at hand. A small direct regression network already gives the lowest squared error on held-out storms, so a generative model has to earn its cost through the part of the future that the regression smooths away. We present TyphoonWorld, a discrete-token world model that generates only that part. Conditioned on tokens of the regression forecast, the latest frames and the best-track state at forecast time, it samples residual fields lead by lead, and members add these residuals to the regression center. We compare it under one protocol with per-pixel Gaussian networks, a diffusion model of the same residuals, residuals from other storms and an unconditional token world model, on 276 forecast windows from 46 held-out storms of Digital Typhoon. TyphoonWorld matches the squared error of the regression, lowers the CRPS of the area colder than 220 K, a direct measure of deep convection, by 14 to 39% against every other ensemble, and ties its spread to forecast error as closely as the Gaussian network, with a correlation of 0.78 across windows.
