We investigate the role of Poisson subalgebras, establishing that flatness of the canonical connection forces two-step nilpotency and yields a linearized evolution equation upon quotienting by the center. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a Poisson splitting and derive the corresponding tangential and transversal evolution equations. Under suitable reductivity assumptions, we show that their non-linear coupling is governed by the curvature of the canonical principal connection on the homogeneous space $G/H$. These results reveal the interplay between the algebraic structure of F$_\text{man}$-Lie groups and the geometric dynamics of hydrodynamic-type equations.

papers.title: Quantum Data Processing Unit for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum device and its controller. Its core is a machine-learned quantum data model (QDM), adapted to the measurement response and noise characteristics of the device. We implement an FPGA pipeline for neutral-atom array assembly that performs occupancy detection and rearrangement scheduling in FPGA logic. One calibrated matched-filter lane classifies a $50\times50$ array in 12.5 $μ$s. An atom-loss model using a software reference planner evaluates a $35\times35$ target with a 60 s trap lifetime and 0.1% loss per moved atom. Removing an assumed 150 ms host round trip raises the predicted assembly success from 8% to 85% and reduces the wall-clock time per successful assembly from 19 s to 0.16 s. A GPU-based outer loop is proposed for refitting model parameters between runs. Its NVQLink transport is measured on the board: over 10 GbE to an NVIDIA DGX Spark, the median FPGA-to-host-to-FPGA round trip is 2.74 $μ$s for 128-byte messages forwarded by a CPU core. A separate 12-bit learned qLDPC kernel is placed and routed for the same FPGA target, with a derived latency of 0.84 ms per round for a $[[1122,148]]$ lifted-product code under code-capacity noise. A quantised GraphMP ranking kernel for the same code runs on the board with a median host-to-FPGA-to-host latency of 50.5 $μ$s with one shot in flight, excluding host-side BP+OSD post-processing. Together, these implementations illustrate a shared architecture with workload-specific models and timing requirements.

papers.title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
papers.abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

papers.title: Classifier-Guided Latent Diffusion for Small-Molecule Generation
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have emerged as a promising class of generative models for molecular design because of their ability to learn complex chemical distributions and support conditional or guided generation. In this work, we investigate a latent diffusion pipeline for property-guided small-molecule generation. The proposed framework represents canonicalized SMILES strings using a frozen ChemBERTa encoder, trains a Transformer-based decoder to reconstruct SELFIES strings from molecular latent embeddings, and learns an unconditional denoising diffusion model in the ChemBERTa latent space. To enable property-directed generation, a differentiable latent property predictor is used to guide the diffusion sampling process. Generated SELFIES strings are converted to SMILES, validated using RDKit, and evaluated using molecular validity, uniqueness, novelty, and predicted property scores. We study guidance toward two drug-relevant binary endpoints: blood--brain barrier permeability and inhibition of human $β$-secretase 1. The results suggest that latent diffusion over pretrained molecular embeddings can generate chemically valid and novel molecules while enabling controllable steering toward desired molecular properties.

papers.title: DART ejecta reveal the recoil momentum budget of a kinetic impact
papers.abstract: Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) demonstrated that ejecta recoil enhances asteroid deflection, but the ejecta processes generating and distributing this recoil remained unclear. We reconstruct three-dimensional ejecta evolution from time-resolved morphology and brightness observations, recovering previously missing constraints on momentum transfer and material transport. Integrating reconstructed momentum yields momentum enhancement factors $β_\mathrm{D}=2.13 \pm 0.19 (1σ)$ for Dimorphos and $β_\mathrm{sys}=2.04 \pm 0.19 (1σ)$ for the Didymos system. Combined with the measured deflection, the reconstructed recoil constrains Dimorphos's bulk density to $1435.18_{-153.71}^{+112.59} \mathrm{kg m^{-3}}$ without assuming its mass. By linking observed orbital deflection to the released material, this reconstruction provides ejecta-based constraints for assessing kinetic-impact effectiveness and investigating how natural collisions drive mass loss and debris transport among small Solar System bodies.

papers.title: Stress peaks and rupture in star-polymer networks with bidisperse arm lengths
papers.abstract: The tensile response of phantom star-polymer networks with bidisperse arm lengths is examined by energy-minimization simulations. Short and long precursors form short-short, short-long, and long-long strands within one end-linked network. The contrast among these strands, composition, functionality, and reaction conversion are varied, and their effects on network rupture are examined. At a large length contrast, two stress peaks appear over part of the composition range. In such realizations, short-short strands carry most of the stress at the first peak, while short-long strands carry most of it after the intervening stress drop. Interesting findings are i) that the peak stretches, including those in double-peak cases, follow composition-dependent master curves when plotted against cycle-rank density, as in monodisperse networks, and ii) that a recently proposed mechanical model describes their cycle-rank dependence, with parameters that vary with composition and arm-length contrast. The parameters differ between the peak series, although their separate determination is limited in some conditions. In addition, the Mark-type improvement of the mechanical properties of the networks by adding a fraction of short strands is discussed. With the implemented FENE force law, the work up to the global stress peak is closer to the long-only value, but an improvement above that reference is not statistically resolved.

papers.title: Vector bundles on spin Kähler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
papers.abstract: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin Kähler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an existence theorem for singular Fueter sections and multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten solutions that holds for every Riemannian metric on a large class of 4-manifolds.

papers.title: Binarization as an Attack Surface in Weightless Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Weightless Neural Networks (WNNs) are lightweight classifiers that binarize their inputs and learn by storing binary patterns in lookup memories, which makes them attractive for resource-constrained tasks such as intrusion detection. Because a small perturbation that crosses no binarization threshold leaves the binary input unchanged, WNNs may appear naturally robust to adversarial examples; a perturbation that does cross a threshold, however, can still change the prediction. We study this tension in WiSARD, the canonical RAM-based WNN, and in two variants that replace its memories with Bloom filters, Bloom WiSARD and BTHOWeN. A continuous perturbation reaches these classifiers only by crossing an encoding threshold, changing at least one binary tuple, and redirecting a memory query; we formalize this mechanism with a threshold-crossing bound and a response-margin certificate for standard Boolean WiSARD. Controlled MNIST experiments compare linear and data-driven thermometer encodings under model-agnostic sensitivity probes, a score-based Simulated Annealing attack, and surrogate-transfer attacks. Changing only the encoding while keeping each model otherwise fixed shows that encoding granularity can trade a small clean-accuracy loss for a large decrease in attack success. On the Bot-IoT, CICIDS, and UNSW-NB15 intrusion-detection datasets, adversarial perturbations lead WNN detectors to classify many attacks as normal traffic and to raise false alarms, even when their aggregate accuracy remains high.

papers.title: Entanglement-to-Stress Relation from an Effective Holographic Description of the Transverse-Field Ising Model
papers.abstract: We investigate an effective holographic description of the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM). We reconstruct the spatial metric from its entanglement entropy and determine the temporal metric using the Einstein-scalar equations, ultraviolet time normalization, and a smooth, horizonless center. Holographic renormalization then gives an enthalpy density that can be expressed through the entropy curvature at half the system size. This relation is a prediction of the effective gravity for the microscopic theory. We test it against the exact finite-size TFIM stress, which is not used in the reconstruction. Away from criticality, the gravity prediction agrees closely with the exact stress in the near-critical scaling regime. This result suggests an entanglement-to-stress relation in the massive Ising field theory, whose field-theoretic derivation remains open. We also find that the reconstructions for different system sizes and couplings share a common scalar potential, up to finite-size deviations near the center that move away as the size increases. This supports the view that the reconstructed geometries are solutions of a single effective Einstein-scalar theory.

papers.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation
papers.abstract: Rapid progress in text-to-audio (TTA) generation demands reliable and explainable automatic evaluation. However, existing metrics fail to simultaneously deliver high correlation with human judgments and meaningful, audio-grounded explanations, forcing reliance on labor-intensive human evaluation that bottlenecks model development iteration. To address this, we propose CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator for text relevance (REL) and audio quality (OVL). Following a reason-then-predict paradigm, CoTTAGE first generates an audio-grounded rationale to diagnose errors before predicting scores. Supported by over 10K newly collected human OVL annotations, CoTTAGE is first trained via supervised fine-tuning and then refined with reinforcement learning using a Thurstone-based preference objective that converts sampled score distributions into pairwise preference probabilities and rewards agreement with rankings derived from human judgments. Across six benchmarks spanning REL and OVL, CoTTAGE achieves state-of-the-art correlation with human judgments while producing human-preferred explanations to accelerate TTA development.

papers.title: A large ultrafilter number at $\aleph_ω$
papers.abstract: Gitik constructed a model where $\aleph_ω$ is strong limit, $2^{\aleph_ω}=\aleph_{ω+2}$ and every strongly uniform ultrafilter on $\aleph_ω$ has character $\aleph_{ω+2}$. We show that in fact every uniform ultrafilter on $\aleph_ω$ has character $\aleph_{ω+2}$ in that model.

papers.title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
papers.abstract: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

papers.title: Quantum spin-wave statistics and dimensionality in thermally activated magnetic transitions
papers.abstract: A quantum correction to the rate of thermally activated transition between magnetic states is formulated within harmonic transition state theory and the Kramers-Langer theory by employing quantum statistics for stable spin-wave excitations around the initial state and the transition state. Quantum spin-wave statistics modifies both parameters of the Arrhenius expression for the transition rate relative to their classical values: the zero-point fluctuations renormalize the energy barrier, while the Bose-Einstein occupation of the spin-wave modes modifies the pre-exponential factor. Comparison of the classical and quantum-statistical pre-exponential factors reveals a systematic error associated with the excessive weight assigned to high-frequency excitations by classical equipartition. This error accumulates over the spin-wave spectrum and becomes increasingly severe with increasing dimensionality of the system. The effect is demonstrated for coherent magnetization reversal, and transitions involving noncollinear magnetic textures, including collapse of a magnetic skyrmion and rupture of a skyrmion tube, where classical and quantum-statistical predictions for the transition rate can differ by many orders of magnitude in three-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
papers.abstract: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets, including disconnected sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.

papers.title: What LLM Agents See and What Users Say
papers.abstract: Before an LLM agent cancels a reservation or deletes a folder for a user, what stops it from acting on a false assumption: what its tools show, or what the user says? In this work, we study this gap with presupposition theory from linguistics: an agent may act only if each claim behind the act (e.g., one reservation fits the name) is seen to hold, answered by the user, or disclosed while the act can be undone. A simple bound shows that when lookups cannot tell one record from two, any agent acts without asking first as often with two records as with one. We then vary whether a search lists, counts, or omits a second match, and whether the user states a claim that a record refutes (e.g., "It is empty"). Under a role-only prompt, a count of a second record leaves most of 36 earlier agents acting on the one they see, whereas listing both stops most. When the user says a record such as a folder is empty, however, a count of its one item stops agents about as often as a listing, and stating the claim mostly cuts acting when it is false. The newest Claude and GPT models always open a counted second record, then never act. When we add a same-name, same-zip customer to a retail benchmark, a lookup returning that customer first led to wrong-account writes in about a quarter of conversations, and one that checks a street the user knows kept completion near the one-customer level. Safe writes therefore need lookups that list or check competing records, and evaluations that vary what tools show.

papers.title: AI-guided robotic in situ fabrication of curvature- and tissue-adaptive wireless bioelectronics
papers.abstract: Personalized bioelectronic devices for wound therapy require not only conformal fabrication on complex body surfaces but also functional adaptation of their electrical characteristics to individual wound geometries. Here, we present an AI-guided robotic in situ printing platform for fabricating wireless wound electrotherapy devices directly on transparent wound dressings. The system integrates a 3D vision camera, a six-degree-of-freedom robotic arm, direct-ink-writing, and geometry-aware RF design optimization. AI-based wound segmentation is used to determine wound dimensions and local surface curvature, while the reconstructed three-dimensional geometry is incorporated into the electromagnetic design of the receiving coil and interdigitated electrodes. In contrast to conventional approaches that use surface geometry only for trajectory generation, the proposed method accounts for both anatomical curvature and tissue dielectric loading to compensate for geometry-induced shifts in resonant behavior. A printable silver ink was characterized in terms of rheology, dimensional reproducibility, electrical resistance, and electromechanical stability, and was used to fabricate multilayer wireless devices directly on curved polyurethane dressings. Wireless power transfer, impedance characteristics, and electric-field delivery were evaluated experimentally and numerically. Finally, robotic in situ fabrication was demonstrated on an anthropomorphic tissue-equivalent forearm phantom, where the measured dielectric properties of the phantom were incorporated into the RF optimization, enabling resonant operation near the target frequency of 25 MHz. This work establishes a perception-to-design-to-fabrication framework for geometry-adaptive wireless bioelectronics and provides a technological foundation for future physical-AI-enabled manufacturing of personalized on-body electrotherapy devices.

papers.title: Polarization of strongly lensed gravitational waves as a probe of the lens-induced orientations of electromagnetic counterparts
papers.abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a well-established phenomenon in electromagnetic (EM) observations, where the lensed images and arcs are resolved on the two-dimensional sky and constrain the mass distribution of the lens. Strongly lensed gravitational waves (GWs) are also expected to be detected routinely by next-generation detectors, but their multiple images are recorded only as one-dimensional time series without positions. Among them, lensed binary neutron star mergers can be accompanied by EM counterparts with resolvable structures, such as relativistic jets. In EM lensing, the lens-induced change in the apparent orientation of such a structure can be measured only relative to other images or statistically, because its intrinsic orientation is not directly observable. In this work, we show that the GW polarization, which the lens leaves unchanged, provides this missing reference, i.e., a compass, so that the orientation offset of each image can be measured in absolute terms. We place this orientation layer on the EM image plane together with image positions from the lensed host arcs and Fermat-potential heights from GW time delays and magnifications. Using a mock population of such mergers observable by the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, we find that the predicted image positions and arrival times are calibrated once the detection selection is included. The lens-induced orientation offsets reach tens of degrees and are detectable in up to a third of the events, at viewing angles above about $40^\circ$ for quadrupole-dominated signals.

papers.title: A counterexample to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a unital \(σ\)-weakly closed subalgebra \(\mathfrak A\) of a von Neumann factor \(\mathcal M\) of type \(\mathrm{II}_1\), whose diagonal is \(\mathfrak D=\mathfrak A\cap\mathfrak A^*=\mathbb CI\). We show that there exist uncountably many faithful normal conditional expectations from \(\mathcal M\) onto \(\mathfrak D\) with respect to each of which \(\mathfrak A\) is a maximal subdiagonal algebra. Let \(τ\) denote the unique normalized faithful normal trace on \(\mathcal M\). The conditional expectation associated with \(τ\) preserves this trace, whereas none of the other conditional expectations is preserved by any nonzero finite trace on \(\mathcal M\). This gives a negative answer to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras in \emph{Amer. J. Math.} \textbf{89}(1967), 578--642.

papers.title: Dynamics of a single 3D vortex ring
papers.abstract: We study the axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flow without swirl originating from a circular vortex ring. For each fixed $s\in(0,1)$ and sufficiently large circulation Reynolds number $Γ/ν$, we prove that, on the time scale $t\lesssim T_{\rm adv}(Γ/ν)^{s}$, the vorticity $ω_θ$ is approximated by a traveling wave solution featuring a Gaussian-type core with scale $O(\sqrt{νt})$, whose off-axis distance remains constant and which continuously translates along the axial direction. In particular, the leading-order axial translation velocity is given by the Kelvin-Saffman formula. The proof relies on the approximation and Arnold energy framework of Gallay and Šverák \cite{GS2024}. We modify the weight used in \cite{GS2024} and estimate the relative-vorticity error to obtain favorable boundary dissipation at the symmetry axis and close the energy estimate.

papers.title: A Unified Device-Level Physical Framework for DRAM Read Disturbance
papers.abstract: Read disturbance in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) depends on both local device interactions and the electrical conditions imposed by shared array circuitry. Here, we combine DIMM-level characterization results, device measurements, and TCAD simulations to interpret RowHammer, RowPress, and ColumnDisturb within a unified device-level physical framework. We relate charge evolution at the floating storage node to three key mechanisms: trap-assisted electron migration (EM), capacitive coupling (CC), and sense-amplifier-mediated disturb (SAMD). EM is local and trap-sensitive, while CC weakens with wordline separation. SAMD extends disturbance through shared column circuitry by modifying unselected-cell leakage under rail-level bitline biases, a contribution supported by the approximately ninefold higher OFF-state leakage measured relative to retention-like conditions for a high-voltage storage state. These distinct spatial ranges account for localized RowHammer and RowPress failures and remote ColumnDisturb populations with abrupt changes at subarray boundaries. We further interpret prolonged RowPress activation as a transition from an initial RowHammer-like transient to sustained leakage driven mainly by SAMD under held wordline and bitline biases. Within this device-level framework, trap effectiveness and storage-state-dependent leakage provide an interpretation of previously puzzling failure signatures, including the earlier onset of 0-to-1 RowHammer failures despite the predominance of 1-to-0 failures at high hammer counts. The same framework explains the observed RowPress and ColumnDisturb polarities and the duration-dependent reversal of neighboring- and passing-wordline effectiveness. These results provide a physical basis for developing compact DRAM reliability models across access patterns and array configurations.

papers.title: Complete Center Classification of a Quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-Equivariant System via Rational Descent and Ramification
papers.abstract: We develop a new structural method to completely classify the elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant system. The method overcomes the computational bottleneck of direct focus-quantity elimination by combining a Liénard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis. We obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, including all degenerate and boundary cases. Sufficiency is established constructively through integrating factors, first integrals and explicit reversible realizations.

papers.title: Generated Evaluation Suites as Diversity-Driven Search for Real Agent Regressions
papers.abstract: Generating an evaluation suite from an agent's specification is diversity-driven search: a generator fills a descriptor space (requirements $\times$ personas $\times$ scenario kinds), and the suite it emits is an archive, then scored like a benchmark by its mean pass rate, which throws away the search's product. We inject 7 controlled defects into a $τ^2$-bench agent across two domains. Coverage yields a ceiling: if a defect's traced footprint holds $b$ scenarios that pass at baseline, it can itself contribute at most $b/N$ to a suite of $N$. For 4 of 5 traceable defects that ceiling lies at or below the detection threshold $θ= 0.10$, so no within-footprint effect can move the suite past it; in both domains the tool-removal defect destroys every covered scenario it can (exactly its ceiling) while the suite-level pass rate moves the other way. Defects split into two regimes: trace-aligned ones, where per-cell scoring recovers the tool-removal defect in full and reveals a second as a significant improvement, and trace-orthogonal ones, whose footprint is behavioural: forced escalation is detected in retail at a traced coverage of exactly zero. Diversity along the generator's own axes helps only where it aligns: at fixed suite size a happy-path-only suite detects nothing, while a kind-diverse one detects the orchestration defect in 5 of 20 draws. Evaluation archives should be scored per cell and should publish coverage as a first-class property.

papers.title: On the Utility of Pre-Trained Visual Representations for Policy Learning of Contact-Rich Insertion Tasks
papers.abstract: Visuomotor imitation learning has become a predominant paradigm for real-world robotic manipulation, yet it remains data-inefficient and brittle to task-irrelevant visual shifts. Pre-trained visual representations promise to ease this burden by distilling priors from internet-scale data, but the ``right'' representation for robotics remains unresolved: existing studies span broad but sparse task distributions and reach conclusions that vary and even conflict, pointing to strong task and setting dependence. We examine this question by bringing a magnifying glass to a common contact-rich manipulation task: insertion. We compare representations from widely used vision foundation models against an explicit contact-centric representation on two closely related insertion tasks, perturb each along controlled axes of occlusion and physical tolerance, and test whether conclusions transfer to the real world. Task dependence proves to be more subtle than previous, broadly scoped evaluations revealed: the best representation differs even between our near-identical tasks, and small changes shift trends in unpredictable ways. Despite this variability, results across simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate the distinct value of spatially-grounded, and in particular, contact-centric information for contact-rich policy learning, while underscoring how difficult it is to estimate such cues reliably under realistic visual complexity and sensor noise. We hope these findings motivate further study of representations in contact-rich manipulation, along with advances in contact perception and its integration into visuomotor policy learning.

papers.title: A mesh-free deep energy method for phase-field modeling of thermally driven brittle fracture
papers.abstract: Phase-field simulation of thermally driven fracture requires resolving localized crack bands whose paths are unknown in advance and thermal boundary layers whose thickness evolves during the transient. Neural energy-based computations of thermal fracture have so far started from defects placed in advance. This paper proposes a mesh-free deep energy method based on multiresolution neural representations that predicts spontaneous crack nucleation, crack spacing, and selective crack propagation and arrest under transient thermal loading. Two networks, each with its own multiresolution encoding, represent the displacement and phase fields and the transient temperature, and the mechanical energy and the incremental functional of the backward Euler heat equation are estimated on integration points redrawn at every iteration. Restricting irreversibility to the crack set, carrying the optimizer state across load steps and decaying the learning rates within each step help prevent spurious damage accumulation. On two notched plates the initiation peak loads agree closely with an independent finite element reference. On a quenched glass strip under an analytical temperature field the crack path changes from straight to oscillatory and then to branched, with an oscillation threshold close to the linear stability prediction. Under a prescribed boundary temperature a quenched ceramic slab forms a crack array of the type observed in experiment, with a spacing close to that of a published benchmark. On the slab and a quenched annulus the arrays are denser than those of a finite element computation on the same material field. No crack paths, nucleation sites or crack-adapted meshes are prescribed.

papers.title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation
papers.abstract: Multi-view 3D transformers such as VGGT reconstruct a scene from a set of unposed images in a single forward pass, predicting camera poses, depth and 3D points, but the cost of their global attention grows quadratically with the num- ber of images. Accelerators borrowed from large language models assume that each token attends to only a few oth- ers; on these models they lose accuracy or gain little speed. We study the global attention of three multi-view transform- ers on seven datasets and find that every layer plays one of three roles: it averages over the whole scene, matches points across many images, or anchors on the first image, whose coordinates the outputs use. Building on this anal- ysis, we propose Regime-AWare ATTention Approximation (RAWATTA), a training-free method that runs attention in 8- bit precision and keeps 16-bit precision only in the layers where a worst-case calibration check requires it. Its fast set- ting, RAWATTA-Fast, also approximates attention in a few averaging and anchoring layers, while matching layers and the first image keep all their keys. On a 12 GB GPU at 50 im- ages, RAWATTA runs VGGT faster than the released code, mostly through our CUDA engine, and loses at most about one point of pose accuracy (AUC@3) on any dataset; RAWATTA-Fast is slightly faster and less accurate. Both fit 200 images, where the released code runs out of memory at 100.

papers.title: Calibrated Period-Luminosity Relations for Mira variables in the Large Magellanic Cloud in the Vera C. Rubin Observatory $zy$-band Photometric Systems
papers.abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space Time (LSST) is expected to discover numerous Mira variables in nearby galaxies, enabling their application for the cosmic distance scale. Miras are excellent distance indicators at infrared wavelengths, and therefore their period-luminosity (PL) relations in reddest $zy$ photometric systems will be crucial in the LSST era. We present first empirical $zy$-band PL relation for 85 oxygen-rich (O-rich) Miras located in the Large Magellanic Cloud based on time-series observations collected using the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) at the Víctor M. Blanco 4-m Telescope. The DECam photometry was directly calibrated using the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 2 (DP2) data. The observed PL relations were found to exhibit a break around a period of $\sim 300$ days, and therefore we only derived and calibrated the PL relations for Miras with a period shorter than $300$ days. We also explored the Rubin LSST DP2 data for known Mira variables in three Local Group dwarf galaxies. The $zy$-band light curves of Miras in IC 1613 are too sparsely sampled, whereas the DP2 observations of NGC 6822 and the Sagittarius Dwarf Irregular Galaxy cover only a short temporal baseline. For an O-rich Mira in NGC 6822, we obtain a distance modulus $μ= 23.32\pm0.24$~mag in good agreement with the literature. Significantly improved temporal coverage is expected in the first official Rubin LSST data release that will enable a robust validation of the PL relation in these nearby systems.

papers.title: Machine-learning charge density for electronic materials and devices simulation
papers.abstract: We present a machine-learning (ML) charge density model, DeltaChargeNet, integrated with the full-potential tight-binding muffin-tin orbital (FP-TB-MTO) method for electronic structure and quantum transport simulations of materials and devices. The ML model predicts electron density from atomic structures with low linear-scaling cost, while FP-TB-MTO provides an accurate tight-binding representation of the system Hamiltonian. To achieve high-fidelity ML density for complex devices with interfaces and disorder, we train an equivariant graph convolutional network to predict $Δρ$-the difference between DFT and atomic superposition densities-under a charge neutrality constraint required for inhomogeneous systems. A secondary ML residual charge model compensates for errors in the primary $Δρ$ model. The predicted density is then used within the full-relativistic FP-TB-MTO framework combined with the non-equilibrium Green's function method. We validate our method on bulk HgCdTe disordered alloys (including vacancy defects) and Au/HgCdTe/Au disordered devices. The maximum band energy error is below 10 meV for bulk HgCdTe. For devices, the charge neutrality constraint suppresses long-wavelength charge bias that would otherwise distort the electrostatic potential by 0.68-1.88 eV near the device center, while residual compensation corrects the remaining 0.16-0.46 eV potential mismatch, essential for reproducing the correct potential barrier profile. Together, these corrections reproduce the layer-resolved potential, including interface steps and bulk-like plateaus, within 0.1 eV of fully self-consistent DFT. Finally, we demonstrate quantum transport in a 11220-atom infrared detector. By combining first-principles accuracy with linear-scaling inference, DeltaChargeNet enables large-scale device simulations without the full DFT self-consistent field loop.

papers.title: Joint World Action Models through Differentiable Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Joint world action models (WAMs) generate future actions and states together, modeling world-action trajectories rather than actions alone. However, trajectory imitation does not ensure that these trajectories are task-effective or consistent with dynamics. We present \textbf{world action trajectory optimization (WATO)}, which optimizes generated actions and future states jointly for control. WATO uses both as references in a dynamics-constrained trajectory optimization problem and differentiates the task loss through the optimized trajectory to train the generator. This makes generated trajectories task-aware and dynamics-consistent while using trajectory optimization only during training. At deployment, WATO directly generates candidate trajectories and ranks them with a world model, without iterative trajectory optimization. Across $7$ visual control environments, WATO improves average success from $79.9\%$ for the imitation joint WAM to $91.7\%$, outperforming strong model-based, goal-conditioned RL, and generative control baselines. Compared with cross-entropy method (CEM), WATO is on average $11.5\times$ faster and uses $600.5\times$ fewer world model evaluations at deployment.

papers.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
papers.abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.

papers.title: The Gaps Between the $Δ$-Unknotting Number and Its Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $u^Δ(K)$ denote the $Δ$-unknotting number of a knot $K$, and let $a_2(K)$ denote the second coefficient of the Conway polynomial. It is known that $u^Δ(K)\geq |a_2(K)|$. We define the $Δ$-gap of $K$ by $G^Δ(K):=u^Δ(K)-|a_2(K)|$. In this paper, we investigate the behavior of this invariant for various families of knots. For example, we prove that the $Δ$-gap of the pretzel knot $K=P(2s, 4s-1,4s+1)$, where $s$ is a positive integer, satisfies $G^Δ(K) \geq 4s$. Consequently, the $Δ$-gap is unbounded. To further investigate the structure of the $Δ$-gap, we distinguish between $Δ$-moves that increase $a_2(K)$ and those that decrease it, since each $Δ$-move changes $a_2(K)$ by $\pm1$. We analyze how these two types of moves contribute to the $Δ$-gap. We also investigate the gaps between $u^Δ(K)$ and other knot invariants that provide lower bounds for it. In particular, we establish explicit formulas and lower bounds for these gaps for certain families of pretzel knots, torus knots, two-bridge knots, and Montesinos knots. Our results show that these gaps can be arbitrarily large. In addition, we identify prime positive knots with $u^Δ(K)=2$ or $3$, and propose a conjecture on a lower bound for $u^Δ(K)$ for prime positive knots.

papers.title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
papers.abstract: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<f<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

papers.title: Auditing Chatbots for Incursion into Professional Legal Practice
papers.abstract: The provision of legal advice has long been in the exclusive jurisdiction of licensed attorneys-a boundary that unauthorized practice of law (UPL) doctrine maintains to protect the public from incompetent counsel. We argue that this boundary is being redrawn, not by courts or bar authorities, but by frontier AI companies. While early chat models were trained to avoid dispensing legal advice, modern models have been reconfigured to reduce refusals and prioritize helpfulness. We ask whether chatbots increasingly do tasks that require a law degree and bar admission, and whether this is harmful in high-stakes legal domains. We develop UPLBench, a benchmark derived from court decisions finding UPL in high-stakes legal domains (e.g., immigration, family law). We then audit 23 chatbot models dating from 2023 to present, evaluating whether chatbots refuse or provide substantive legal advice, and whether they refer users to lawyers or legal aid. Unlike prior work that aims to establish the legal capabilities of chatbots (e.g., bar exam performance), our approach converts legal doctrine into a testable benchmark for evaluating chatbot adherence to law. We find modern chatbots increasingly perform tasks courts reserve for lawyers and decreasingly recommend that users consult lawyers. Subject matter expert attorneys reviewing our transcripts identified interaction patterns, such as failure to elicit relevant facts, that would be considered inadequate counsel. If acted upon, such advice could lead to deportations, loss of homes, and family separations-the very harms that UPL rules are designed to protect against. We weigh paths forward to protect the public, including compelling models to comply with existing law. We call upon the legal profession to respond to this incursion into its domain of expertise as there are insufficient protections and remedies for users who rely on chatbot legal advice.

papers.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
papers.abstract: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads. To address this requirement, we introduce AscendGYM, a benchmark whose initial suite comprises 48 kernels across three difficulty levels. Each kernel is paired with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes are collected from real-world training and inference tasks. Consequently, performance improvements on AscendGYM map directly to the corresponding workloads. In terms of usability, two evaluation modes are supported in AscendGYM: model evaluation and model-harness evaluation. The kernel optimization capabilities of both trained models and custom agents are allowed to be measured. It provides a complete execution environment that closely reproduces how Ascend kernels are invoked in practical pipelines. For model evaluation, it additionally includes a built-in harness equipped with search orchestration and experience accumulation. Finally, we propose a new metric, the Speedup-Token Score (STS), which quantifies performance gains relative to token cost. By jointly considering speedup and cost, STS enables the assessment of practical kernel optimization capability of a model or harness under an acceptable budget. AscendGYM is available at https://github.com/SLAI-AITP/AscendGYM.

papers.title: Safety Side Effects of Preventative Persona Steering: An Empirical Audit
papers.abstract: High-level behaviors such as sycophancy and hallucination correspond to directions in a model's activation space (Chen et al., 2025). These directions, known as persona vectors, can suppress undesirable traits either at inference time, subtracting the vector during generation, or through preventative steering, adding the vector during fine-tuning, so the optimizer never needs to encode the trait in weights, then removing the vector at evaluation. Chen et al. (2025) recommend preventative steering because it preserves Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) accuracy, but validations of this recommendation have measured capability alone. We primarily evaluate results on preventative steering of sycophancy and hallucination vectors on three models, measuring three safety benchmarks alongside trait expression, coherence, and MMLU. Our findings show that preventative steering still changes refusal behavior, but by an amount that depends on the trait and does not establish that preventative persona steering is safety-neutral, and steering methods should be evaluated on several safety benchmarks.

papers.title: TouchTwin: Scaling Human Touch Data via Real-to-Sim-to-Real
papers.abstract: Human demonstrations are becoming the main source of data for dexterous manipulation, and real-to-sim-to-real pipelines multiply each demonstration in simulation. These pipelines rebuild the interaction from vision, which recovers how the hand moves. Which fingers touch, when, and how hard remain unobserved, because a hand pose shows where each finger stops on the surface rather than how far it is driven to close. This gap is a force gap: on held-out recordings, a hand policy that imitates the observed pose grips with 0.31x the recorded force, and a policy trained on physics replays of vision-tracked poses grips with 1.55x. TouchTwin closes the gap with measured human touch. Each selected TouchScale recording, captured with head and wrist RGB-D cameras and an 880-taxel glove, is rebuilt in MuJoCo. Coding agents write the objects as physics-tested programs, and a per-subject tactile hand replays the interaction with the recorded touch setting the contact and the closing force of each finger. In simulation, a policy trained on touch-grounded replays grips at 0.99x the recorded force and succeeds in 20/20 trials on held-out recordings and 35/36 unseen perturbations; a contact predictor trained on them misses 13% of real contact frames, against 32% for vision-based replays. Each replay also seeds perturbed demonstrations with simulated contact and force labels, rendered as realistic video in new views and scenes.

papers.title: Lean-PEP: Performance-Estimation Certificates to Formally Verified Algorithmic Bounds
papers.abstract: Performance-estimation certificates describe worst-case bounds for optimization algorithms. Turning a certificate into a formal theorem requires exact verification of its algebra and a connection between its coordinates, constraints and objective and the intended function-level problem. Lean-PEP provides a reusable interface for this task. It checks a submitted source and exact certificate against a supported canonical finite model, and a parameterized analytic theorem transfers the resulting finite bound to every admissible algorithm trajectory. Generated computation proofs discharge the obligations that depend on each certificate. An additional capture entry checks the numerical record and reconstruction policy. The implemented two-step proximal-gradient consumer verifies a new input with normalized bound 62500/499999, and a fixed eight-configuration batch yields seven distinct payloads with accepted certificates and executed Lean proofs. PG/GD cases and one-step attainment witnesses establish the corresponding algorithmic conclusions, and a fresh installation reproduces consumption of the supplied input. These results show how new certificate data can reuse a proved analytic interface to obtain function-level bounds within the supported models.

papers.title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics
papers.abstract: Predicting plastic flow in body-centered cubic metals across temperature and strain-rate regimes requires distinguishing structural resistance from kinetic contributions. Here, we develop a temperature dependent mobility law for screw dislocation, integrating thermal activation theory and relativistic effects. Through discrete dislocation dynamics simulations, uniaxial tension and compression simulations were conducted on configurations with different initial dislocation densities, elucidating the correlation between plastic strain rate and key parameters such as stress, temperature, and dislocation density. Subsequently, a unified constitutive model incorporating temperature and strain rate is derived based on microscopic mechanisms. The model naturally bridges microscopic mechanisms to continuum response, resolving the additivity dilemma by establishing explicit physical criteria for how structural resistances and competing kinetic mechanisms superimpose. Through rigorous bottom-up simulations, we quantitatively capture the crossover point where phonon drag overtakes thermal activation, providing a mechanism-based explanation of anomalous thermal hardening. This work enables physically consistent predictions of strength and creep behavior across broad temperature and strain-rate regimes, advancing beyond phenomenological descriptions toward transparent, mechanism-based alloy design.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Cluster Lifecycle Management: Deciding When and How to Evolve Behavioral Clusters
papers.abstract: Behavioral clusters learned over user or item interactions drift as behavior evolves: some fragment into sub-behaviors, some converge, some disappear, and new patterns emerge. Two paradigms dominate the maintenance of evolving clusterings. Threshold triggers fire a pre-specified action when a hardcoded statistic crosses a cutoff; refit-and-track (MONIC-style) re-clusters every window and infers transitions from how the new clusters align with the previous window's. Both hardwire the decision into a threshold or a re-clustering rule. We study an alternative in which a large language model (LLM) makes the lifecycle decision in place. Given a threshold-free, whole-population view of the current cluster set (statistical health, labels, member texts, residual mass), the LLM decides per cluster whether and how to act (split, merge, retire, create, or no-action) without re-clustering. Because the useful signal channel depends on how informative the labels are, we fix a richness-conditioned policy in advance: statistics when label distinctiveness is low, fused statistics+semantics when it is high. On three public datasets spanning label richness (YooChoose 0.17, MOOC 0.50, News-Category 0.70), the policy-selected LLM mode obtains the highest F1 on all three, with far fewer interventions and stronger restraint than tuned threshold heuristics and a MONIC steelman (paired Wilcoxon p <= 0.003, bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero). The gain is concentrated more in precision than recall. The useful modality shifts from statistics to semantics/fusion as richness rises. Semantics hurt on YooChoose, fusion is roughly neutral on MOOC, and the semantic channel is required on News. One base prompt template and one fixed policy serve all three datasets, whereas the tuned baseline collapses when moved between them. We treat this shift as a practitioner diagnostic observed on three datasets, not a validated law.

papers.title: Data-driven exploration of the strength-ductility synergy in refractory high-entropy alloys
papers.abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) have attracted increasing attention for their exceptional ability to retain strength at high temperatures. However, current research mainly concentrates on compositions close to equimolar alloys, leaving a large part of the composition space unexplored. Here, we develop a multiscale framework based on a data-driven dislocation genome method that constructs energy landscapes for edge dislocation motion across various compositions. The local configurational force derived from the energy landscape is incorporated into dislocation dynamics simulations, revealing a scaling law connecting macroscale strength and atomic-scale local resistance governed by fluctuations in the local configurational force. Based on this scaling law, a new solid-solution strengthening model for edge dislocation in BCC alloys is developed, followed by a data-driven exploration of refractory alloys considering both strength and ductility. The developed method and theory are adaptable, allowing for extension to other BCC alloy systems and guiding high-throughput alloy design.

papers.title: Global saddle selection and exact absolute-instability boundaries for convection in porous media with throughflow
papers.abstract: In the Darcy-Prats problem, horizontal throughflow leaves the temporal onset of convection unchanged but raises the heating required for a localized disturbance to grow at a fixed point. The saddle equations give five candidates, but only the saddles reached by deformation of the Fourier contour contribute to the growth. For $Ra>π^2$, $Pe>0$ we prove that the same off-axis pair contributes throughout the domain: no Stokes transition can change its contribution. Its growth gives a unique analytic absolute threshold, first reached by the lowest vertical mode. Rescaling transfers the selection to Forchheimer drag, transverse rolls of a power-law fluid, anisotropic permeability, an open upper boundary and a vertical magnetic field. A shift of the same growth function accounts for interphase heat exchange in a model of metallic foam. At prescribed throughflow the threshold increases strictly with either resistance coefficient. In particular, a vertical magnetic field raises the absolute threshold at fixed Péclet number. Tabulated thresholds check the reduction. Algebraic elimination gives the boundary polynomial, and frequency recovery selects its physical branch. At the Darcy level the selected saddles trace an arc of the elliptic curve 11a3, a degeneration of a genus-two family at nonzero shifted levels. Series inversion on this arc gives an integer weak-throughflow series and an all-order strong-throughflow expansion. Rational certificates establish the exact convergence radii of both series on the selected sheets.

papers.title: Innovative Integrated Congestion Management Market: Synergizing Operational Flexibility of Transmission System Operators with Aggregator-Driven Resources
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an innovative congestion management market that seeks to integrate and harness the operational flexibility available to Transmission System Operators (TSO) in conjunction with the flexibility offered by aggregators. In the context of operational flexibility, this study investigates Network Topology Optimization (NTO) as a pivotal strategy for to address the transmission network congestion, specifically through the strategic switching of certain buses. To achieve this, an N-1 secured NTO is formulated using a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) methodology. Concurrently, acknowledging the crucial and growing importance of aggregator-provided flexibility in congestion management, the paper presents a novel integrated congestion management market. In this framework, aggregators submit bids, and the TSO, taking into account these bids alongside the potential for the NTO, clears the market with the goal of minimizing the overall cost of congestion management. The proposed integrated market is constructed using a linear optimization model, ensuring its practical applicability in real world scenarios. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed market design are assessed using the standard IEEE 39-bus system, with results indicating promising potential and applicability

papers.title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
papers.abstract: This paper presents a constraint-aware reinforcement learning (CARL) controller for battery energy storage system (BESS) sizing and photovoltaic (PV) ramp-rate smoothing. Rapid PV power fluctuations caused by cloud transitions can introduce operational and stability challenges in power systems. To mitigate these impacts, grid codes impose ramp-rate limits (RRL) on PV power injected to the grid. BESSs can support such grid codes by absorbing or supplying power during rapid variations. However, the extent to which BESSs can reduce PV-induced variability depends on (i) the BESS power and energy capacities; and (ii) the adopted controller. Thus, BESS sizing and controller design are coupled. Conventional moving-average control can increase battery usage due to filter-induced lag, while ramp-rate control is reactive and does not account for the long-term impact of actions on battery state of charge and future ramp events. Optimization-based methods can reduce BESS requirements by anticipating future PV variations, but their performance depends on accurate PV forecasts. To address these limitations, the CARL controller learns a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment. Ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints are incorporated into a causal feasibility interval that guarantees feasible actions by definition. A full-horizon input-convex neural network (ICNN)-based optimization is developed as a noncausal benchmark for the minimum achievable BESS requirements. Evaluation using three real-world PV datasets shows that, at a 10\%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduces peak BESS power by 8.7--10.4\% and energy capacity by 47.5--62.6\% relative to conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining the grid-codes compliance.

papers.title: Pseudo-profiles for vectorial Allen-Cahn systems
papers.abstract: The purpose of the present paper is to present a new type of solutions to the elliptic vectorial Allen-Cahn system of equations. Its main feature is that in the classical rescaling its asymptotics do not follow the rule of balance of energies, which is crucial in the analysis of the asymptotics for the scalar problem.

papers.title: More Agents, More Samples, or More Thinking? Untangling Coordination, Ensembling, and Test-Time Compute in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.abstract: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. This practice confounds coordination with sample multiplicity and inference compute. We synthesize nine primary empirical evaluations comprising 516 unique multi-agent configurations organized along a resource vector R with six dimensions and a baseline ladder with four categories. Against baselines with a single pass (Category A), multi-agent accuracy differences are negative overall and near zero when omitting the largest contributing study. When evaluated against baselines matched on sample count (Category B) or resource budget (Category C), multi-agent systems average -0.042 in accuracy, and multilevel random effects modeling on the log odds scale remains negative across sensitivity checks. Multi-agent accuracy equals or falls below the baseline in 74% of these comparable contrasts, and study means are nonpositive in almost all evaluated studies. Across studies reporting both baselines, moving from a greedy pass to a sampled baseline shifts accuracy differences by -0.038 on average. Because communication adds no information when agents share identical evidence, positive returns require partitioned evidence, external verification, or error diversity across models. We provide a reviewer checklist and accounting utilities.

papers.title: Homogeneous pursuit in $β$ model
papers.abstract: Data in forms of networks has been encountered in various prevalent fields at the arrival of big data era. To unveil and recover the true model with core units with numerous links, the $β$-model under sparsity constraint is proposed to meet the expectation of statisticians and engineers. Not only does this network model inherit spectacular property from the Erdős-Rényi model, but also exhibits degree heterogeneity through tuning sparsity parameter $s$. In this paper, we propose Homogeneous Pursuit (HP), an $\ell_0$-constrained maximum likelihood estimation method implemented through a primal-dual algorithm. To ease the harshness of computation, we find the surrogate function of the corresponding objective function to derive Majorization Minimization algorithm through the primal-dual process. Moreover, after meticulous evaluation, the algorithm brought about captures the property of fine convergence rate in a contraction mapping way. Under some mild conditions, the proposed generalized information criterion (GIC$^*$) for selecting the sparsity level is consistent to find the truth. Combining HP with GIC$^*$ gives the adaptive procedure HP-GIC$^*$; HP-BIC denotes the same estimation method with sparsity selected by BIC. Finally, simulation studies show that GIC$^*$ improves support recovery relative to BIC in the reported comparisons, while HP achieves lower computational cost while maintaining estimation accuracy comparable to the sparse benchmark methods. A microfinance application illustrates the use of HP-GIC$^*$ for studying the association between network prominence and participation, with improved fit in the reported village-level regressions.

papers.title: Neural Simulation-Based Inference for Computational Cognitive Models: A Tutorial
papers.abstract: Computational cognitive modeling is an increasingly essential methodology to elucidate the mechanisms underlying human and animal cognition. By fitting models to empirical data, researchers can perform parameter estimation, model comparison, and model-based neural analyses to assess competing theories, quantify individual differences, and investigate neural representations. Typically, fitting these models relies on likelihood-dependent methods (e.g., Maximum likelihood estimation or hierarchical Bayesian methods). However, for many reasonable cognitive models, computing the likelihood is computationally intractable, in which case these methods become inadequate. This substantially limits the range of theories that researchers can investigate. Simulation-based inference with neural networks (neural SBI) has emerged as a powerful toolkit to overcome this hurdle. By training deep neural networks on datasets generated through model simulations, neural SBI learns the relation between observable data and cognitive models. This approach enables all the applications of standard modeling while bypassing the likelihood computation, without constraints on empirical data size. Despite its successful adoption across diverse scientific fields, neural SBI remains underutilized in cognitive modeling, partly due to a lack of accessible, domain-tailored guidance. This tutorial addresses this gap by providing a clear workflow for applying neural SBI to cognitive models. We also provide practical use cases and recommendations for reducing the computational and simulation burden, facilitating efficient implementation in real-world research settings. By lowering the technical barriers to neural SBI, this tutorial aims to empower cognitive scientists to investigate richer theory spaces and ultimately propel scientific discovery.

papers.title: Selective coupling and spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states under local perturbations
papers.abstract: In this work we investigate the spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states in a one-dimensional structure described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. We show that a local potential applied to the domain wall induces a selective coupling between a topological state and specific bulk states. Moreover, by increasing the gate potential, we observe that the domain wall state energies asymptotically reach a bulk band, whereas new domain wall states appear on the opposite side of the band. As a consequence, the domain-wall-state spectrum evolves through a sequence of localized states that remain separated from the bulk continuum. These effects are also reflected in transport calculations, where the conductance peaks follow the evolution of the energy spectrum. To experimentally verify these phenomena, we realize an RLC topo-electrical circuit and perform impedance spectroscopy measurements. We find that the impedance matches the local density of states, exhibiting resonances at frequencies associated with the bulk energies that selectively couple to the domain wall topological state.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the clamped-plate eigenvalue ratio conjecture
papers.abstract: Ashbaugh in 1999 conjectures that the ball maximizes the ratio of the second to the first eigenvalue for the vibrating clamped-plate problem. We disprove this conjecture by constructing smooth connected domains in every dimension $d\ge2$. The construction starts with an interior sphere on which the displacement is required to vanish. The first two eigenvalues have the same relative increase at first order, but the second increases more at second order. This gives a strict increase of their ratio, which survives approximation of the sphere by finitely many codimension-two supports and their replacement by smooth holes. We identify the limiting Sobolev spaces through trace estimates and logarithmic cutoffs, and use the geometric construction for the buckling problem to obtain connected perforated domains.

papers.title: Choosing Quantized Code LLMs by File Size and Energy per Solved Task
papers.abstract: A developer running a code assistant on a laptop downloads one model file, and local inference moves the energy of every request onto that machine. A common rule says a larger model at lower precision tends to beat a smaller one at higher precision. We ran 24 GGUF files of Qwen2.5-Coder at four sizes on a fanless MacBook Air M2 and priced each in energy per solved task on 542 EvalPlus tasks. The result is a selection guide indexed by Ollama's listed file size, with an evidence label on each pick. At 1 and 2 GB it picks the q4_K_M files of the 1.5B and 3B models, both on the correctness and energy frontier under every accounting. At 3 GB as listed, the larger-model rule picks 7B-q2_K, the only measured 7B file that fits, and there it does not pay. That file brings no significant gain in solves over the 2 GB pick, 3B-q4_K_M, and the 90% CI limits any 3B-q4_K_M deficit to 2.4 points. Yet 7B-q2_K needs 2.03 times the energy per solved task on CPU, GPU and memory rails, or 1.66 to 1.81 times on whole-system power. On HumanEval+, five alternating session pairs give a ratio of 1.925 against 1.956 in the main grid. At 8 GB, 7B-q6_K buys a significant gain over the 2 GB pick at a higher energy price. From 1.5B up, q4_K_M trails the highest precision measured at its size by less than 3 points (90% CI). We release per-task results, power logs and the analysis script.

papers.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

papers.title: Offline KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning with Stochastic Transitions
papers.abstract: KL-regularized reinforcement learning is the objective behind RL fine-tuning of language models, and its data are often collected by the reference policy itself. However, beyond bandits and deterministic transitions, little is known about how much offline data it needs. In this work, we study finite discounted Markov decision processes with unknown stochastic transitions, $K$ state-action pairs and effective horizon $H$. For data that cover the regularized optimum with concentrability $C\geq 4$, every estimator needs $Ω(KCH^3/(ε\max\{ε,β\}))$ samples on some instances when $ε$ is small, where $β$ is the temperature. Under a fixed design, pessimistic soft value iteration with a variance-aware penalty attains this rate with high probability, up to logarithmic factors, when $β\geq 1.4H$. When the data come from the reference policy itself, we show that it covers the optimum up to a power law whose exponent grows as $H/β$; in the same temperature range, this power law alone gives the estimator a sample complexity polynomial in $1/ε$, with no coverage assumption. For $β\geq H$ the power can also increase the sample size needed by a factor polynomial in $1/ε$. Finally, the plug-in estimator, which is minimax optimal with a generative model, can fail on reference data at small temperatures when many actions are rarely seen, while the pessimistic estimator does not.

papers.title: LinearKnot: Linear-Time Approximation of the Pseudoknot Partition Function
papers.abstract: Pseudoknots, where two or more helices cross, are central to many functional RNAs, including frameshifting signals, telomerase RNA, riboswitches and viral genomes. With arbitrary pseudoknots, finding the minimum free energy structure is NP-hard, so most RNA secondary structure prediction tools only consider pseudoknot-free structures. Dirks and Pierce (DP03) pioneered the first pseudoknot partition function, which underlies NUPACK's pseudoknot model, but it takes $O(n^5)$ time and $O(n^4)$ memory, making it practical only for very short sequences. Linear-time approximate dynamic programming, as in LinearFold and LinearPartition, does not transfer easily to DP03: a partial pseudoknot leaves a gap filled by its crossing partner, whose complementary sequence may still lie ahead of the scan, so it cannot be ranked by its inside weight. We present LinearKnot, a linear-time approximation of DP03 in three passes: (a) LinearPartition gives pseudoknot-free weights; (b) a second pass builds tables that estimate each partial stem's crossing partner; and (c) a third scans a left-to-right reformulation of DP03 that reserves the 5' nucleotides in the pseudoknot helix for subsequent pairing, keeping the states with the largest estimated contribution. Without pruning, this reformulation computes DP03's pseudoknot recursion exactly, so the only approximation is which states the beam keeps. End-to-end, time grows linearly ($n^{1.01}$) and memory marginally above linear ($n^{1.15}$) from 1,000 to 9,392 nt. LinearKnot folds the 9,392 nt Rous sarcoma virus genome in 2.4 hours and 90.5 GB, where exact DP03 would need an estimated 40,000 years and 54 million GB, and matches exact DP03 base-pair probabilities on 418 PseudoBase RNAs with a median RMSD of $9.2\times10^{-7}$. Our code is available at https://github.com/gautammilan/LinearKnot.

papers.title: Horizontal component of the ion drag force in a plasma sheath
papers.abstract: The ion drag force is responsible for the underlying physics behind many important phenomena in complex (dusty) plasma, such as void formation, particle alignment in an ion flow, shadow-like attraction between the particles, dust clouds rotation in the presence of a magnetic field etc. In this paper, we investigate the ion drag force acting on particles levitating near the sheath edge of a capacitively coupled discharge in xenon. In particular, we calculate the radial (horizontal) component of the ion drag force directed parallel to the lower electrode above which the particles levitate. The calculation is based on the actual information about the ion flow, which is directly obtained using Laser Induced Fluorescence. The calculated horizontal component is comparable in magnitude to the vertical one, which pushes the particles toward the electrode surface, and is higher than previously expected. This unexpected finding must be taken into account in future research. The very possibility of the measurements we report opens the door for detailed studies of dusty plasma phenomena governed by ions and their flows.

papers.title: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
papers.abstract: Multimodal tabular learning involves classification and regression on tables combining structured numerical and categorical features with unstructured text and images. These unstructured fields are commonly represented by pretrained encoder embeddings reduced with principal component analysis (PCA). This reduction prioritizes input variance but may overlook information relevant to predicting the target. We introduce LightTAR, a simple, inexpensive method that adapts dimensionality reduction to the prediction task. LightTAR augments the standard PCA representation with a few target-aware features extracted jointly from the final and an intermediate encoder layer using regularized partial least squares (PLS). We evaluate LightTAR with 21 tabular models, including tree ensembles, neural networks, and tabular foundation models. LightTAR improves average predictive performance for all models and, averaged across models, improves prediction on almost every MulTaBench dataset. These gains come with a small increase in total runtime relative to PCA representations. LightTAR integrates directly into existing encoding pipelines, improving tabular learners' predictive performance without modifying the encoder or the learner.

papers.title: Multiple spontaneous otoacoustic emissions as a single standing wave unstable to modulation
papers.abstract: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) have been interpreted either as cochlear standing waves or as local oscillations of hair cells. Multiple SOAE lines test both views, because each view must explain how the lines coexist. In the standing-wave view, each line is a separate resonance. In the intermodulation view, some lines are distortion products of others. Both explanations assume several independent oscillations. Independent oscillations, however, compete through the saturating cochlear amplifier, and the dominant oscillation suppresses the others. The saturation has another role besides suppression. The saturation also induces an oscillation of the gain at twice the frequency of the oscillation. In lasers, this oscillation of the gain, called the \textit{pump}, creates sidebands. This paper examines whether a cochlear standing wave can pump the gain by itself. A two-dimensional cochlear model with a step in the gain produced a single standing wave. The pump destabilized a pair of lines near the neighboring resonances. The other lines were phase-locked intermodulation products of the main line and the pair. A group of equally spaced SOAEs can thus arise from one self-sustained oscillation. The spacing follows the resonances of the standing wave, and the two explanations can hold together.

papers.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
papers.abstract: Long-horizon navigation from indoors to outdoors remains an open problem for humanoid robots: one instruction covers rooms, doors and roads, and the camera moves with the gait. Worken, AGIBOT's measure of productive robot work, depends on robots that reach their workplaces autonomously. We present X-Nav, to our knowledge the first system to take a bipedal humanoid through a language-instructed long-horizon mission from indoors to outdoors. X-Nav covers a pipeline from data to deployment. Its data engine collects navigation data in open-source scenes, in digital twins of deployment sites and on real robots. Its navigation model, MELIOR, takes only RGB images from the robot's built-in camera and comes in two versions: MELIOR-A predicts actions, and MELIOR-N predicts a navigation goal. Its agentic workflow, X-Navarch, turns a brief human instruction into sub-tasks and deploys MELIOR on the robot with explicit target navigation and obstacle avoidance. On the Lingxi X2, X-Nav completes a mission of about a hundred metres from an office lobby to a store in a neighbouring building; LiDAR and odometry are used for target approach and low-level control. The mission is completed with both versions of MELIOR: the robot follows a change of destination and walks through a door from the lobby to the road, and with X-Navarch it also passes static and dynamic obstacles on the route. During deployment, MELIOR is adapted with data collected in a digital twin of the site; the adaptation raises its closed-loop success rate in the twin, and the adapted model is then deployed on the robot at the real site. In addition, MELIOR achieves competitive results on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks.
